Gemini on Google Pixel Watch

How to use Gemini on your Google Pixel Watch

With Gemini on Google Pixel Watch, you can turn your smartwatch into a smart, helpful, and personalized companion. Gemini will help you navigate your day as an always-available assistant, all from your wrist.

Activate Gemini on your watch

To use Gemini on your watch, make sure:

  • Gemini is set as your digital assist app on your connected phone.

  • To use Gemini in an eligible language and region.

  • Your Pixel Watch apps are up to date.

To confirm Gemini is installed on your watch:

  • Press and hold the button located above the crown on your watch.

    • If Gemini is installed and set up, it should launch directly or prompt you to complete the setup process for Gemini.

  • Press the crown on your Pixel Watch. This will open your app list.

    • Scroll through the list of applications on your watch and tap Gemini.

    • If Gemini is installed, you’ll find it as an app.

Once activated, you can open Gemini on your watch in a couple of ways:

  • Press and hold the button located above the crown on your watch.

  • Tilt your wrist and use the hotword “Hey Google.” Your watch screen needs to be active to use the hotword.

  • Tap on the Gemini complication on your watch face.

  • Pixel Watch 4: Get help from Gemini by raising your wrist and speaking without saying “Hey Google”. Your watch will show a mini glow on the bottom of the watch face to indicate that you’re ready to speak. Learn more about Raise-to-Talk on Pixel Watch 4.

    • Tip: The watch must be close to your mouth before you talk.
    • To enable this feature: On Google Pixel Watch, tap Settings and then Gestures . Then, turn on Raise to talk.

Tip: To handle some actions related to apps in Gemini, check individual apps settings on your mobile device. Learn how to use and manage apps in Gemini.

Customize your watch with Gemini

Add shortcuts to your Gemini tile to quickly access actions.

  1. Swipe to the Gemini tile on your watch face.

  2. Tap Add new Gemini actions.

  3. Choose or create: You can either pick from recommended actions or create your own custom action.

    • Create custom action: If you choose to create your own, tap the Mic or Keyboard. From there, you can define actions such as open your music app, set a timer, and more.

  4. Confirm Action: Once you’ve created or chosen an action, a confirmation prompt will appear. Tap the check mark to save it.

Track your workouts and daily stats with your voice with Gemini

Use Gemini to start and control your workouts or check your health metrics with your voice. Press and hold the button above the crown or say “Hey Google” to ask Gemini to perform actions like:

  • Control your exercise: Start, pause, resume, or end an activity. For example, say “start my run.”

  • Get your live health metrics: Ask “What’s my heart rate?” or “What’s my step count?” to check your current stats in the Fitbit Today app.

Use Smart Replies with Gemini on your Pixel Watch 4

Use Smart Replies to send personalized and accurate replies with just one tap on your Pixel Watch 4. Learn how to use Smart Replies on Google Pixel Watch.

How do I set a timer or use the stopwatch on my Fitbit device?

Time events using the stopwatch feature on your Fitbit device, or use the countdown timer to keep track of elapsed time.

Ace 2, Ace 3, Inspire, Inspire HR, and Inspire 2

Time events with the stopwatch

  1. On your device, open the Timers app .
  2. If you used the countdown timer previously, swipe down and tap the stopwatch icon .
  3. Tap the play icon to start the stopwatch.
  4. Tap the pause icon to stop the stopwatch.
  5. To reset the stopwatch, swipe down and tap Reset. Press the button or buttons to exit.

Keep track of elapsed time with the countdown timer

  1. On your device, open the Timers app .
  2. If you used the stopwatch previously, swipe up and tap the countdown icon .
  3. Swipe to choose the number of hours, then tap to set the hours. To set a timer for less than an hour, choose 00 hr.
  4. Swipe to choose the number of minutes, then tap to set the minutes.
  5. Tap the play icon to start the timer.
  6. To reset the timer, swipe down and tap Reset. Press the button or buttons to exit.
  7. Your device vibrates when the time allotted is done.
Blaze

Time events with the stopwatch

  1. On your tracker, navigate to the Timer screen and then tap it. The stopwatch is the first option.
  2. Tap the screen and then tap the play button to start.
  3. Tap the pause button to end.
  4. Tap the arrow in the top right to reset the stopwatch, or press the left button on your tracker to exit.

Keep track of elapsed time with the countdown timer

  1. On your tracker, navigate to the Timer screen and then tap it.
  2. The stopwatch is the first option. Swipe to choose the countdown timer.
  3. Tap the screen and then tap 0:00 to set the timer.
  4. Press the left button to return to the countdown screen.
  5. Tap the play button to start. Your tracker flashes and vibrates when the time allotted is done.
Charge 2

Fitbit Charge 2 has a stopwatch feature. To time events with the stopwatch:

  1. On your tracker, navigate to the Stopwatch screen.
  2. Press and hold the button to start the stopwatch.
  3. Press and hold the button to stop.
Charge 3, Charge 4, Versa, Versa Lite Edition, and Versa 2

Time events with the stopwatch

  1. On your device, open the Timer app.
  2. If you used the timer previously, swipe right to choose the stopwatch feature.
  3. Tap the play icon to start the stopwatch.
  4. Tap the pause icon to stop.
  5. Tap the reset icon to reset the stopwatch.

Keep track of elapsed time with the countdown timer

  1. On your device, open the Timer app.
  2. If you used the stopwatch previously, swipe left to choose the countdown timer.
  3. Tap the screen, then swipe up or down to set the timer.
  4. Press the left button to return to the countdown screen.
  5. Tap the play icon to start. Your device flashes and vibrates when the time allotted is done.
  6. Tap the check mark icon or press the button to stop the alert.

The stopwatch and timer can run at the same time.

Note that timers you set in the Timer app on Fitbit Versa 2 are separate from timers you set with your voice assistant. For more information on using your voice assistant to set timers, see How do I use a voice assistant on my Fitbit smartwatch?

Charge 5, Charge 6, Inspire 3, and Luxe

Keep track of elapsed time with the countdown timer

  1. On your device, swipe left or right to the Timers app and tap to open it.
  2. Swipe up or down to choose the number of minutes, then tap to set the minutes. To set a timer for less than a minute, choose 00 minutes.
  3. Swipe up or down to choose the number of seconds, then tap to set the seconds.
  4. Tap the play icon to start the timer. Your device vibrates when the time allotted is done.
  5. Swipe up to dismiss the alert.

Time events with the stopwatch

  1. On your device, swipe left or right to the Timers app , then swipe up and tap Stopwatch .
  2. Tap the play icon to start the stopwatch.
  3. Tap the pause icon to stop.
  4. Swipe up and tap the reset icon to reset the stopwatch.

The stopwatch and timer can run at the same time.

Sense and Versa 3

Time events with the stopwatch

  1. On your device, open the Timer app .
  2. Tap 0.0.
  3. Tap the play icon to start the stopwatch.
  4. Tap the pause icon to stop.
  5. Tap the reset icon to reset the stopwatch.

Keep track of elapsed time with the countdown timer

  1. On your device, open the Timer app .
  2. Tap Add Timer.
  3. Swipe up or down to set the timer.
  4. Tap the time to start the timer. Your device flashes and vibrates when the time allotted is done.
  5. Tap the check mark icon or press the button twice to stop the alert.

The stopwatch and timer can run at the same time.

Note that timers you set in the Timer app are separate from timers you set with your voice assistant. For more information on using your voice assistant to set timers, see How do I use a voice assistant on my Fitbit smartwatch?

Sense 2 and Versa 4

Time events with the stopwatch

  1. On your device, open the Timers app .
  2. In the Stopwatch section, tap Start.
  3. Tap the play icon to start the stopwatch.
  4. Tap the pause icon to stop.
  5. Tap the reset icon to reset the stopwatch.

Keep track of elapsed time with the countdown timer

  1. On your device, swipe left or right from the clock face to find the Timers tile.
  2. Tap a timer to start it.
    1. If the duration you want isn’t listed, tap the menu icon and then Add Timer.
    2. Swipe up or down to set the timer.
    3. Tap the time to start the timer.
  3. You can navigate away from the tile while the timer is running. Return to the Timers tile to see the progress of your timer. Press the pause icon to pause the timer or the X icon to cancel it. Your device flashes and vibrates when the time allotted is done.
  4. Tap the check mark icon or press the button to stop the alert.

The stopwatch and timer can run at the same time.

Note that timers you set in the Timers app are separate from timers you set with your voice assistant. For more information on using your voice assistant to set timers, see How do I use a voice assistant on my Fitbit smartwatch?

How do I set up and troubleshoot apps on my Fitbit device?

Note that the apps available vary based on your device.

How do I set up apps on my Fitbit device?
Alexa

Use the Alexa app on Sense, Sense 2, Versa 2, Versa 3, and Versa 4 to check the weather, set timers and alarms, start a workout in the Exercise app , control your smart home devices, and more. For more information, see How do I use a voice assistant on my Fitbit smartwatch?

Clocks

Switch between 5 saved clock faces with the Clocks app . For more information, see How do I change the clock face on my Fitbit device?

Google ECG

For help with the Google ECG app , see What is the Google ECG app?

EDA Scan

For help with the EDA Scan app , see How do I track & manage stress with my Fitbit device?

Find Phone

When you can’t find your phone, use the Find Phone app to locate it.

Requirements:

  • Your Fitbit device must be connected (“paired”) to the phone you want to locate.
  • Your phone must have Bluetooth turned on and be within 30 feet (10m) of your Fitbit device.
  • The Google Health app must be running in the background on your phone.
  • Your phone must be turned on.

To find your phone:

  • Open the Find Phone app on your Fitbit device.
    • Sense and Versa 3—swipe left on the clock face.
    • Sense 2 and Versa 4—while on the clock face, press the button.
    • Charge 5, Inspire 3, and Luxe—swipe down on the clock face.
  • Tap Find Phone. Your phone rings loudly.
  • When you locate your phone, tap Cancel to end the ringtone.
Google Assistant

Use the Assistant app on Sense and Versa 3 to check the weather, set timers and alarms, control your smart home devices, and more. For more information, see How do I use a voice assistant on my Fitbit smartwatch?

Google Maps

Get turn-by-turn directions on your wrist with the Google Maps app on Charge 6, Sense 2 and Versa 4. For more information, see How do I use Google Maps on my Fitbit device?

Philips Hue

To control your lights with your Philips Hue system and Fitbit watch, your Philips Hue system must be connected to the same Wi-Fi network as your phone, and your watch must be within Bluetooth range of your phone.

Note for Android users: Due to recent Android security changes, your local network must be using one of the following IP address ranges: 192.168.0.0/24 or 192.168.1.0/24.

To set up the Philips Hue app:

  1. Open the Philips Hue app on your watch.
  2. The app starts searching for your Hue bridge. When prompted on your watch, press the pairing button on your bridge to complete the pairing process.

To adjust your lights from your watch:

  1. Open the Philips Hue app on your watch.
  2. From the Rooms screen, tap on or off to adjust all the lights in each room. Up to 10 rooms are listed. If you have more than 10 rooms, use the Philips Hue app on your phone to adjust additional rooms.
  3. Tap the and then icon next to a room to see the lights in that room.
    • Tap the checkbox next to each light to turn it on or off.
    • Swipe left to view the Scenes screen. Tap a scene name to set it.

To add new devices, rename lights, customize scenes, or organize the lights in each room, use the Philips Hue app on your phone.

Spotify

For help with the Spotify app , see Control music with my Fitbit device.

Starbucks

The Starbucks app is only available in the United Kingdom, United States and Canada. To load your Starbucks card into the app:

  1. Open the Google Health app .
  2. At the top left, tap Connections and then your device and then Watch faces.
  3. Tap your device’s tab and then Starbucks Card and then Settings.
  4. Add your Starbucks gift card or Starbucks Rewards program number.
  5. To make a purchase, open the Starbucks app on your watch and hold the watch face near the reader.

To remove your Starbucks card from the app:

  1. Open the Google Health app .
  2. At the top left, tap Connections and then your device and then Watch faces.
  3. Tap your device’s tab and then Starbucks Card and then Settings.
  4. Tap your card number.
  5. Tap the X.
  6. After your number turns gray, tap Save.

Visit starbucks.com or use the Starbucks mobile app to register your card, check your card balance, view rewards, or reload your card.

Strava

The Strava app is no longer available in the Google Health app. Use the Strava app on your phone to track your workouts. For more information on connecting your Fitbit account with Strava, see Connect third-party devices and apps to the Google Health app.

Tile

For help with the Tile app , see What should I do if I lose my Fitbit device?

Uber

To set up the Uber app:

  1. If you don’t have an Uber account, download the Uber app on your phone and follow the on-screen instructions to create an account.
  2. Open the Google Health app .
  3. At the top left, tap Connections and then your device and then Watch faces.
  4. Tap your device’s tab and then Uber and then Settings.
  5. Tap Login to be redirected to the Uber login page.
  6. Sign in to your account and follow the on-screen instructions to log in to your account and authorize the connection.
  7. Use the Uber app on your phone to set any preset locations, such as your home or work address. For instructions, see Uber’s help article.

To request a ride:

  1. Open the Uber app on your watch.
  2. Your watch uses your preset home and work addresses as your default pickup and destination locations. If needed, tap the swap icon to swap the pickup and destination addresses. To change your pickup location, tap it and select a different address. You can select your current location, detected using your phone’s GPS signal, or a recently used address.
  3. After selecting the correct pickup and destination locations, tap Confirm.
  4. The cost of the trip, estimated time of pickup, and estimated time of arrival are shown. Swipe left or right to select a service. Tap Request to request the ride.
  5. When a driver confirms the ride, the driver’s information appears. Swipe up to see the estimated time until pickup and cancel the ride if needed.
  6. To change your destination address or rate your driver, use the Uber app on your phone.
Weather

To set up the Weather app:

  1. Open the Google Health app .
  2. At the top left, tap Connections and then your device and then Watch faces.
  3. Tap your device’s tab and then Weather and then Settings.
  4. By default, the Weather app shows your current location, which can’t be deleted. Add up to 2 additional locations you want to see in the Weather app.
  5. Sync your device with the Google Health app. It can take a few minutes to see the updated list of locations on your device.

If the weather doesn’t update, check the following settings:

  • Location services must be turned on for the Google Health app. For instructions, see Use GPS on your Fitbit device or Pixel Watch.
  • The Google Health app must remain running in the background on your phone.

If you change locations, sync your device to see your new location in the Weather app.

To change the units used for the temperature in the Weather app:

  1. Open the Google Health app .
  2. At the top left, tap Connections and then your device and then Watch faces.
  3. Tap your device’s tab and then Weather and then Settings.
  4. In the Temperature Unit section, tap Units and choose the unit you want to use.
YouTube Music

Use YouTube Music controls on Charge 6 to control YouTube Music on your phone. Navigate between playlists, skip or replay songs, and adjust the volume from your tracker. For more information, see Control music with my Fitbit device.

How do I troubleshoot apps on my Fitbit device?

  1. For apps to access the internet, your phone must be nearby with the Google Health app running in the background and Bluetooth turned on. Many apps require internet access.

  2. Check if the app has a pending update. For instructions, see How do I install and manage apps on my Fitbit device?

  3. Turning off app permissions can cause the app to stop functioning. Check that all permissions are turned on:

    1. Open the Google Health app .
    2. At the top left, tap Connections and then your device and then Watch faces.
    3. Tap an app to open it.
    4. Tap Permissions.
    5. If any permissions are turned off, turn them on. Note that some permissions can cause your phone to use more data.
    6. Tap Save.
    7. If you see a caution icon next to the app in the My Apps tab, check the following permissions on your phone:
      • Location services must be turned on for the Google Health app. For instructions, see Use GPS on your Fitbit device or Pixel Watch.
      • Calendar access must be turned on for the Google Health app:
        • On iPhones, open the Settings app on your phone and then Google Health and then make sure Calendars is turned on.
        • On Android phones, open the Settings app on your phone and then Apps and then Google Health and then Permissions and then Calendar and then make sure the access is set to Allow.
        • On Windows 10 phones, open the Settings app on your phone and then Privacy and then Google Health and then make sure Calendar access is turned on.

  4. Fitbit Sense, Fitbit Versa, Fitbit Versa 2, and Fitbit Versa 3 must be connected to Wi-Fi for some larger apps and clock faces to install or update. For more information, see How do I connect my Fitbit watch to Wi-Fi?

  5. For additional troubleshooting instructions, contact the app developer.

    For Fitbit- or Google-developed apps, contact Customer Support.

How do I take on-wrist phone calls with my Fitbit smartwatch?

Use the built-in speaker and microphone in Fitbit Sense, Fitbit Sense 2, Fitbit Versa 3, and Fitbit Versa 4 to take calls from your wrist.

For information on receiving phone call notifications on your watch, see Change phone notifications on my Fitbit device.

How do I set up on-wrist calls on my Fitbit device?

If you didn’t set up on-wrist calls when you connected your Fitbit device to your account:

  1. Open the Google Home app .
  2. At the top left, tap Connections and then your device and then On-Wrist Calls.

Follow the instructions below to set up on-wrist calls.

Android

Tap each setup requirement, and follow the on-screen instructions to accept and turn on the necessary pairing permissions and requests.

  • Note that if you see a See Instructions button, you might be using an older version of the Google Health app. Tap See Instructions, and use the to set up on-wrist calls.
  • On Sense and Versa 3, if you don’t see a pop-up message to turn on device controls when you tap Bluetooth Pairing:
    1. Open the Settings app on your watch and then Vibration & Audio. In the On-wrist calls section, tap Sense Controls/Calls or Versa 3 Controls/Calls.
    2. On your phone, tap Settings and then Bluetooth. Your phone scans for available devices.
    3. When you see Sense Controls/Calls or Versa 3 Controls/Calls as an available device, tap it. A number appears on your phone screen.
    4. When the same number appears on your watch, tap Pair.
    5. Return to the Google Health app on your phone. The Bluetooth pairing step is complete.
iPhone
  1. Tap Start Setup.
    • On Sense and Versa 3, if you’re unable to start the on-wrist call setup, open the Settings app on your watch and then Vibration &Audio. In the On-wrist calls section, tap Sense Controls/Calls or Versa 3 Controls/Calls, and then proceed to the next step.
  2. On your phone, tap Settings and then Bluetooth. Your phone scans for available devices.
  3. When you see the name of your Fitbit device follows by the word “Controls”or “Calls” (for example, Sense 2 Calls) as an available device, tap it. A number appears on your phone screen.
  4. When the same number appears on your watch, tap Pair.
  5. Return to the Google Health app on your phone. Tap Done to complete setup.

Note: You might need to update your Fitbit device to the latest firmware version to turn on this feature. For more information, see Update your Fitbit device.

How do I answer a call on my Fitbit watch?
  1. When you receive a phone call, tap the green phone icon on your watch. Note that your phone must be nearby with the Google Health app running in the background.
  2. Speak into your watch to talk to the other person. You hear their voice from the speaker on your watch.
    • To adjust the volume of the speaker, tap the speaker icon and then minus icon or plus icon . Swipe right to return to the previous screen.
    • To mute yourself, tap the microphone icon . Tap the same icon to unmute yourself.
    • To switch to a keypad, tap the 3 dots icon and then Keypad. Swipe right to return to the previous screen.
  3. To end the call, tap the red phone icon .
How do I switch an on-wrist call to my phone?
  1. During an on-wrist call, tap the 3 dots icon and then Phone to move the call to your phone.
  2. To move the call back to your watch, tap the watch icon .

Note that if you answer a call with your phone, you can’t switch the call to your watch.

Why don’t on-wrist calls work on my Fitbit device?

If you can’t answer on-wrist calls, check the following requirements:

  • Make sure you’re using the latest version of the Google Health app. For more information, see Explore the Google Health app.
  • Make sure your Fitbit device is up to date. For more information, see Update your Fitbit device.
  • Keep your phone nearby with the Google Health app running in the background. Your phone should be within 30 feet (10 meters) of your watch.
  • Call notifications must be turned on. For more information, see Change phone notifications on my Fitbit device.

If you continue to have issues, try the following troubleshooting steps:

  1. On your phone, turn Bluetooth off and back on.
  2. Restart your Fitbit device. For instructions, see Restart your Fitbit device
  3. Remove your Fitbit device’s controls or calls from the list of Bluetooth devices on your phone.
  4. Set up on-wrist calls again. For instructions, see

Note that your Fitbit device’s controls or calls might be listed as “Not Connected” in the list of Bluetooth devices on your phone. When you receive a phone call, the controls automatically reconnect. This feature requires more frequent charging.

How do I use a voice assistant on my Fitbit smartwatch?

Check the weather, set timers and alarms, control your smart home devices, and more by speaking to a voice assistant on Fitbit Sense, Fitbit Sense 2, Fitbit Versa 2, Fitbit Versa 3, and Fitbit Versa 4.

Over the coming weeks we’ll be progressively phasing out Google Assistant on Sense and Versa 3. This means that Google Assistant voice control for activities will no longer be available on your Fitbit device. You can learn more about this process here.

You can still continue to use Amazon Alexa voice assistant on your Fitbit devices. For more information check

Amazon Alexa is only available in certain languages and countries at this time. Check

To learn about the Assistant experience on mobile upgrading to Gemini check The Assistant experience on mobile is upgrading to Gemini.

How do I set up a voice assistant on my Fitbit smartwatch?
Amazon Alexa Built-In
  1. Open the Google Health app .
  2. At the top left, tap Connections and then your device and then Voice Assistant.
  3. Tap Amazon Alexa and then Sign in with Amazon and then Get Started.
  4. Create or log in to your Amazon account.
  5. Tap Close to return to the Voice Assistant tile.
How do I interact with a voice assistant on my Fitbit smartwatch?
  1. Open the Alexa app on your watch.
    • Note that the Google Health app must be running in the background on your phone.
  2. Say your request. Your voice assistant responds with text on-screen and through the watch’s speaker with Sense 2 or Versa 4.
    • To adjust the speaker volume, tap the speaker icon (Alexa) and then - icon or + icon.

You don’t need to say “Alexa” before speaking your request. For example:

  • Set a timer for 10 minutes.
  • Set an alarm for 8:00 AM.
  • What’s the temperature outside?
  • Remind me to make dinner at 6:00 PM.
  • How much protein is in an egg?
How do I check the alarms, reminders, and timers I set with a voice assistant on my Fitbit smartwatch?
Amazon Alexa
  1. Open the Alexa app on your watch.
  2. Tap the alerts icon in the top right then swipe left or right to navigate between alarms, reminders, and timers.
  3. Tap an alarm to turn it on or off. To adjust or cancel a reminder or timer, tap the Alexa icon and say your request.

Note that the alarms and timers you set with Alexa are separate from those you set in the Alarms app or Timer app .

Which countries and languages are supported by Alexa Built-in on Fitbit?
  • Alexa Built-in
  • North, Central, and South America United States (English) Canada (English) Canada (French) Mexico (Spanish) Argentina (English) Chile (English) Colombia (English) Costa Rica (English) Peru (English) Europe Austria (German) France (French) Germany (German) Ireland (English) Italy (Italian) Netherlands (English) Poland (English) Spain (Spanish) Sweden (English) United Kingdom (English) Asia India (English) Japan (Japanese) Australia and New Zealand Australia (English) New Zealand (English)
How do I change the language my voice assistant recognizes?
Amazon Alexa
  1. Open the Google Health app .
  2. At the top left, tap Connections and then your device.
  3. Tap Voice Assistant and then Amazon Alexa.
  4. Tap the language you’re currently using, and then choose a new language from the list.
How do I disconnect my voice assistant?
Amazon Alexa
  1. Open the Google Health app .
  2. At the top left, tap Connections and then your device.
  3. Tap Voice Assistant and then Amazon Alexa and then Log Out.
Is my voice assistant always listening?

No. The microphone in your watch only turns on when you activate it, for example by opening a voice assistant app. The microphone turns off when the voice assistant responds, when you close the voice assistant, or when your watch’s screen turns off.

Does Google Health collect or use my voice data when I use a voice assistant?

No. Google Health doesn’t collect any voice data or audio clips from your watch.

How do I enable more skills for Alexa on my Fitbit watch?

For added functionality, install the Amazon Alexa app on your phone. With the app, your watch can access additional Alexa skills.

Add the Fitbit skill to ask Alexa to open the Exercise app or start a workout for you.

  1. In the Amazon Alexa app on your phone, find the Fitbit skill.
  2. Tap Enable.
  3. Log in using your Fitbit account credentials and give permission for Alexa to access your profile and data.

To ask Alexa to open the Exercise app on your watch, set up the Fitbit skill for Alexa. For more information, check These commands are currently available in English, German, French, Italian, Spanish, and Japanese.

Tip: Saying “Alexa” doesn’t activate your voice assistant on your watch. You must activate your voice assistant before the microphone in your watch turns on.

Check amazon.com for more information about Alexa skills.

What should I do if my voice assistant doesn’t work on my Fitbit smartwatch?
  • The Alexa option doesn’t appear in the Google Health app.
    • Solution: Alexa on your Fitbit device is only supported in certain countries. Check .
  • I can’t sign in to my Amazon account during setup.
    • Solution: Clear the cookies on your phone: For iPhones, check support.apple.com . For Android phones, check Clear cache & cookies . Try again to set up Alexa in the Google Health app.
  • “Connection Lost” error
    • Solution: Keep your phone within 30 feet of your watch. Open the Google Health app on your phone and sync your watch. The Google Health app must remain running in the background on your phone for your voice assistant to work.
  • “No Internet” error
    • Solution: Your phone must have an internet connection, either through Wi-Fi or a cellular data signal.
  • “Set Up Alexa” error
    • Solution: . If you already set up Alexa, sync your watch.
  • When setting an alarm or reminder with Alexa, my time zone is incorrect.
    • Solution: To change the time zone Alexa uses, follow the instructions on amazon.com .
  • When I ask Alexa for directions, Alexa can’t get my exact location.
    • Solution: Turn on location services: Allow the Google Health app to use your phone’s location. For more information, check Use GPS on your Fitbit device or Pixel Watch Allow Alexa to use your phone’s location. Follow the instructions on amazon.com . In the Amazon Alexa app on your phone, make sure Location services are turned on, and “Device Location” is correct. Tap either setting to change it. Note that not all countries support location information.
  • The reminder I set with Alexa doesn’t show whether it’s recurring in the list of reminders on my watch.
    • Solution: Each reminder only shows the next time you’ll receive it, not whether it’s recurring. However, if you set a reminder as recurring, you’ll receive it on the schedule you set.
  • My alarm, notification, or reminder didn’t alert me.
    • Solution: Charge your watch and try again. If your watch’s battery is below 8%, your watch won’t vibrate.
  • I can’t cancel the alarm, reminder, or timer I set with Alexa. or The alarm, reminder, or timer I set with Alexa doesn’t show up on my watch.
    • Solution: Log out of Alexa, then log back in: Open the Google Health app . At the top left, tap Connections and then your device. Tap Voice Assistant and then Amazon Alexa and then Logout . After you log out, tap Amazon Alexa and then Login with Amazon . Follow the instructions to log in. Try again to check or cancel your alarm, reminder, or timer.
  • My voice assistant uses the wrong language.
    • Solution: .
  • My voice assistant has trouble understanding me.
    • Solution: If you recently went for a swim or got your watch wet, there might be water in the microphone. Wait a few minutes for the microphone to dry, then try again to use your voice assistant.
  • Alexa asks, “What skill do you want to learn about?” in response to every request.
    • Solution: Say “Exit” to leave the skill interaction. Alexa will respond to your next request.

How do I use Google Maps on my Fitbit device?

No matter where the day takes you, get turn-by-turn directions on your wrist with Google Maps on Fitbit Charge 6, Fitbit Sense 2, and Fitbit Versa 4.

How do I set up Google Maps on my Fitbit device?
  1. Open the Google Health app .
  2. At the top left, tap Connections and then your device.
  3. Tap Apps and then Google Maps tile.
    • If you see a message that the Google Maps app isn’t installed on your phone, tap the app store link to download it.
  4. Tap Install and select the permissions you want to grant. For the best experience, select all.
    • Note that if you use the Google Health app on an iPhone, you must tap Allow when prompted to give Google Maps access to use Bluetooth.
  5. You will see a check mark on your Fitbit device confirming the app was installed.
What is auto-start and how do I turn it on or off?

When auto-start is turned on, the Google Maps app automatically opens on your Fitbit device when you start navigation on your phone. By default, auto-start is turned on for cycling and walking navigation and off for driving navigation. To adjust the auto-start setting:

On-device (Sense 2 and Versa 4 only)
  1. From the clock face, press the button to open a list of the apps installed on your watch.
  2. Swipe up until you see the Google Maps app . Tap the app to open it.
  3. Swipe up to find the Auto-start section.
    • Tap the switch to turn the feature on or off.
    • Tap Cycling, Driving, or Walking to turn auto-start on or off for each type of navigation.
Google Health app
  1. Open the Google Health app .
  2. At the top left, tap Connections and then your device.
  3. Tap the Google Maps tile.
    • Tap the switch next to Auto-start to turn the feature on or off.
    • Tap Cycling, Driving, or Walking to turn auto-start on or off for each type of navigation.
How do I start turn-by-turn directions on my Fitbit device?

  1. Open the Google Maps app on your phone, search for the location you want to navigate to, choose your mode of transportation, select a route, and tap Start to begin navigation. For more detailed instructions on how to use the Google Maps app on your phone, check Use navigation in Google Maps. Note that the Google Health app must be running in the background.

  2. If auto-start is turned on for the mode of transportation you selected on your phone, the Google Maps app opens on your Fitbit device automatically. If auto-start isn’t turned on, open the Google Maps app on your Fitbit device. ##### Sense 2 and Versa 4

    1. From the clock face, press the button to open a list of the apps installed on your watch.
    2. Swipe up until you see the Google Maps app . Tap the app to open it.
    3. Tap View to see your current trip.
    Charge 6

    Swipe right from the clock face until you see the Google Maps app. Tap to open it.

  3. During navigation, you can use the app on your Fitbit device to pause or cancel navigation: ##### Sense 2 and Versa 4

    • Swipe up to see the next 2 upcoming navigation steps and your destination location.
    • Tap Preview to prompt the Google Maps app on your phone to display all upcoming steps.
    • Tap Pause navigation on watch to pause navigation on your watch, but continue navigation on your phone. Tap View to resume navigation on your watch.
    • Tap Exit to cancel navigation on your watch and your phone.
    Charge 6
    • Swipe up and tap the pause button to pause navigation.
    • Tap the resume button to resume navigation or the finish button to end navigation.

  4. When you reach your destination using cycling or walking navigation, your Fitbit device shows a summary of your activity. Tap Done to close the Google Maps app.

Do I have to bring my phone with me to use Google Maps on my Fitbit device?

Yes, your phone must remain within Bluetooth range of your Fitbit device to use the Google Maps app.

How do I cancel navigation on my Fitbit device?

During navigation, swipe up in the Google Maps app on your Fitbit device to find the following options:

  • Tap Pause navigation on watch (Sense 2 and Versa 4) or the pause button (Charge 6) to pause navigation on your device, but continue navigation on your phone. Tap View (Sense 2 and Versa 4) or the resume button (Charge 6) to resume navigation on your device.
  • Tap Exit (Sense 2 and Versa 4) or the finish button (Charge 6) to cancel navigation on your device and your phone.
How do I uninstall Google Maps from my Fitbit device?

To disconnect Google Maps from your Fitbit device:

  1. Open the Google Health app .
  2. At the top left, tap Connections and then your device.
  3. Tap the Google Maps tile and then Disconnect Google Maps.

To uninstall the Google Maps app from your Fitbit device:

  1. Open the Google Health app .
  2. At the top left, tap Connections and then your device and then Apps.
  3. Swipe to find the Google Maps app. Tap it.
  4. Tap Uninstall to remove the app from your Fitbit device.
Why isn’t Google Maps working on my Fitbit device?

If Google Maps navigation isn’t appearing on your Fitbit device, try the following troubleshooting steps:

  • Your phone must be connected to your Fitbit device. For more information, go to Why won’t my Fitbit device sync?
  • Check if your Fitbit device has a pending update. For more information, go to Update your Fitbit device.
  • Check if the Google Health app on your phone has a pending update. Please update to the latest version of the Google Health app.
  • Check if the Google Maps app on your Fitbit device has a pending update. For more information, go to How do I install and manage apps on my Fitbit device?
  • If auto-start is turned off, navigation doesn’t automatically open on your Fitbit device. To check a trip you’ve started on your phone, open the Google Maps app on your device. (On Sense 2 and Versa 4, you must then tap View.)

iPhone users should also try the following troubleshooting steps:

  • Make sure Google Maps is installed on your phone and up-to-date. For more information, go to support.apple.com.
  • Restart your phone. For more information, go to support.apple.com.
  • Check that your phone’s Location permission is set to Always for the Google Health app. For more information, go to support.apple.com.
Can I use the Google Maps app on my Fitbit device for public transit directions?

No. The Google Maps app on your Fitbit device can only be used for cycling, driving, and walking directions.

Manage alarms on your Fitbit device

Alarms on your Fitbit device vibrate to gently awake or alert you at a set time.

Important: Alarms you set in the Alarms app on Fitbit Sense, Fitbit Sense 2, Fitbit Versa 2, Fitbit Versa 3, and Fitbit Versa 4 are separate from alarms you set with your voice assistant. For more information on using your voice assistant to set alarms, see How do I use a voice assistant on my Fitbit smartwatch?

Set alarms on your Fitbit device

For Fitbit Charge 3, Fitbit Charge 4, Fitbit Charge 5, Fitbit Charge 6, Fitbit Inspire 3, Fitbit Luxe, Fitbit Sense series, Fitbit Versa series, and Google Pixel Watch series, set alarms on your device. Learn how to set alarms and manage notifications on the Google Pixel Watch.

For all other Fitbit devices, set alarms in the Google Health app.

Tip: Sense, Versa, Versa Lite Edition, Versa 2, and Versa 3 alarms won’t go off if your device has less than 8% battery.

On your Fitbit device
Charge 6
  1. On your device, open the Alarms app. It shows your next scheduled alarms and the option to set a new alarm.
  2. Tap + New Alarm. Swipe up to find this option if you already created multiple alarms.
  3. Set your alarm time.
    1. Swipe up and down to choose the time.
    2. Tap the time to select it.
    3. Tap AM or PM.
  4. Choose to turn on Smart Wake.
    • When enabled, Smart Wake attempts to find the best time to wake you starting 30 minutes before the alarm time you set. It avoids waking you during deep sleep so you’re more likely to wake up feeling refreshed. If Smart Wake can’t find the best time to wake you, your alarm alerts you at the set time.
  5. Choose the days you want to be alerted.
  6. Save your alarm.
    • Swipe right to find your alarms.
Inspire 3
  1. On your device, open the Alarms app. It shows your next scheduled alarms and the option to set a new alarm.
  2. Tap + New Alarm. Swipe up to find this option if you already created multiple alarms.
  3. Set your alarm time.
    1. Swipe up and down to choose the time.
    2. Tap the time to select it.
    3. Tap AM or PM.
  4. Choose to turn on Smart Wake.

    • When enabled, Smart Wake attempts to find the best time to wake you starting 30 minutes before the alarm time you set. It avoids waking you during deep sleep so you’re more likely to wake up feeling refreshed. If Smart Wake can’t find the best time to wake you, your alarm alerts you at the set time.

    • Alarms that use the Smart Wake setting have a different icon than the other alarms on your device.

  5. Choose the days you want to be alerted.
  6. Save your alarm.
    • Swipe right to find your alarms.
Versa 4
  1. On your device, open the Alarms app. It shows your next scheduled alarms and the option to set a new alarm.
  2. Tap + New Alarm. Swipe up to find this option if you already created multiple alarms.
  3. Set your alarm time.
    1. Swipe up and down to choose the alarm time.
    2. Tap AM or PM and the time to set it.
    3. To choose additional days when the alarm should alert you, tap the alarm to edit it further.
  4. Choose to turn on Smart Wake.
    • When enabled, Smart Wake attempts to find the best time to wake you starting 30 minutes before the alarm time you set. It avoids waking you during deep sleep so you’re more likely to wake up feeling refreshed. If Smart Wake can’t find the best time to wake you, your alarm alerts you at the set time.
    • Alarms that use the Smart Wake setting have a different icon than the other alarms on your device.
  5. Choose the days you want to be alerted.
  6. Save your alarm.
    • Swipe right to find your alarms.
Sense 2
  1. Press the button on the side of your device.
  2. Scroll to All apps and then Alarms.
  3. Tap + New Alarm. Swipe up to find this option if you already created multiple alarms.
  4. Set your alarm.
    1. Swipe up and down to choose the alarm time.
    2. Tap AM or PM and the time to set it.
    3. To choose additional days when the alarm should alert you, tap the alarm to edit it further.

Turn on Smart Wake

  1. When enabled, Smart Wake attempts to find the best time to wake you starting 30 minutes before the alarm time you set. It avoids waking you during deep sleep so you’re more likely to wake up feeling refreshed. If Smart Wake can’t find the best time to wake you, your alarm alerts you at the set time.
    • Tip: Alarms that use the Smart Wake setting have a different icon than the other alarms on your device.
  2. Choose the days you want to be alerted.
  3. Save your alarm.
    • Swipe right to find your alarms.
Other devices
  1. On your device, open the Alarms app. It shows your next scheduled alarms and the option to set a new alarm.
  2. Tap + New Alarm. Swipe up to find this option if you already created multiple alarms.
  3. Set your alarm time:
    • Charge 5 and Luxe: Swipe up and down to choose the time, and tap to select it. Tap AM or PM.
    • Sense and Versa 3: Swipe up and down to set the alarm time. Tap AM or PM. When you’re done, tap the time to set it.
    • Charge 4, Versa 2, Charge 3, Versa Lite Edition, and Versa: Tap the time, then swipe to set the alarm time. Be sure to set AM or PM. Press the back button on your device.
  4. Choose to turn on Smart Wake.
    • When enabled, Smart Wake attempts to find the best time to wake you starting 30 minutes before the alarm time you set. It avoids waking you during deep sleep so you’re more likely to wake up feeling refreshed. If Smart Wake can’t find the best time to wake you, your alarm alerts you at the set time.
    • Alarms that use the Smart Wake setting have a different icon than the other alarms on your device.
  5. Choose the days you want to be alerted.
  6. Save your alarm.
    • Charge 5, Luxe, Sense series, and Versa 3: Swipe right to find your alarms.
    • Charge 4, Versa 2, Versa Lite Edition, Charge 3, and Versa: Press the back button to find your alarms.
On the Google Health app
  1. Open the Google Health app . At the top left, tap Connections and then your device.
  2. Go to Alarms.
  3. Tap Add New Alarm.
  4. Select your alarm time.
    1. Tap your preferred time.
    2. If you don’t have a 24-hour clock, tap AM or PM.
    3. Select OK.
  5. Choose to turn on Smart Wake.
    1. When enabled, Smart Wake attempts to find the best time to wake you starting 30 minutes before the alarm time you set. It avoids waking you during deep sleep so you’re more likely to wake up feeling refreshed. If Smart Wake can’t find the best time to wake you, your alarm alerts you at the set time.
  6. Set the days and frequency, then save.

Dismiss alarms on your Fitbit device

Your device vibrates and flashes when a silent alarm goes off. This notification repeats several times or until dismissed. If you don’t dismiss an alarm, it repeats in 9 minutes.

Google Fitbit Air

Firmly double tap your Google Fitbit Air to dismiss or stop a ringing alarm.

To dismiss an alarm, double tap your Google Fitbit Air when it vibrates. If you do not dismiss it, the alarm will snooze for 9 minutes.

Charge 6

Swipe up from the bottom of the screen and tap Dismiss .

To snooze the alarm for 9 minutes, swipe down from the top of the screen or press the button(s).

Inspire 3

Swipe up from the bottom of the screen and tap Dismiss .

To snooze the alarm for 9 minutes, swipe down from the top of the screen or press the button(s).

Versa 4

Tap Dismiss .

To snooze the alarm for 9 minutes, press the button or tap Snooze .

Sense 2

Tap Dismiss .

To snooze the alarm for 9 minutes, press the button or tap Snooze .

Other devices
  • Inspire 2 and Ace 3: Press both buttons on your device.
  • Other devices: Press the button on your device.

Delete or turn off alarms on your Fitbit device

For most Fitbit devices, turn off alarms on your device’s screen. For instructions, go to .

If you can’t adjust alarms on your device’s screen, use the Google Health app. For instructions, go to .

On the Google Health app
Google Fitbit Air

Important: Keep your Google Fitbit Air close to your phone.

  1. Open the Google Health app .
  2. Go to Device Management, then tap Alarms .
  3. Select the alarm you want to delete.
  4. Tap Delete alarm and then Confirm and delete.
Other devices
  1. Open the Google Health app . At the top left, tap Connections and then your device.
  2. Tap Google Health reminders & alerts and then Silent Alarms.
  3. Tap the alarm you want to delete and then Delete Alarm and then Delete Alarm.
On your device

To turn off an alarm:

  1. Open the Alarms app, then tap the alarm.
  2. Turn off the alarm.

To delete an alarm on Charge 4, Charge 5, Charge 6, Inspire 3, Luxe, Sense series, and Versa series:

  1. Open the Alarms app.
  2. Tap the trash icon or Remove.
    • You may need to swipe up to see this option.

What is Google Health Labs

Select users have the opportunity to explore new, experimental capabilities and provide valuable feedback as they’re developed through Google Health Labs also referred to as Labs. These users can find Labs by tapping your Profile and then Labs or at the bottom of the Health tab in the Google Health app. From there, users can either opt-in to try out a lab or join a waitlist.

Testing new capabilities in Google Health Labs will help Google Health learn how users interact with these capabilities and how they can be improved. This helps Google Health provide interesting and actionable information to you about your health and fitness data.

These labs are available for a limited time in Labs. You might need a Google Health Premium subscription or to meet additional eligibility criteria to access them.

How to join Google Health Labs
  1. Open the Google Health app .
  2. Tap your Profile or Initial and then Labs.
  3. Find a lab you are interested in participatiling in and tap Get notified to show you are interested in joining a lab. Each lab within may have additional eligibility requirements. Select users who meet the requirements for the lab will be chosen to participate.
  4. If you’re selected, tap Turn on.
  5. Follow the in-app instructions and complete any consents to join the lab.

How is my data used
All Google Health labs

To join any Google Health Labs, you must turn on the Data shared for health research and product development consent. If you agree, when you use Fitbit products and services, Fitbit and Google will collect your data. This data will be used to research and develop new health and wellness products and services or to support health research.

You may opt out of this consent at any time. For details, refer to .

Individual labs

Google Health Labs is made up of individual labs. These labs may be powered by various technologies, such as large language models, machine learning, and artificial intelligence, which continuously evolve.

You need to opt-in to each lab separately, and some labs may require you to sign an additional consent. Some labs limit your ability to participate in other labs.

Before you join a lab, you’re given information on what data we collect and how we plan to use it. Lab-specific consents may describe additional data that might be collected and how data is used for research and development of products and services, that includes those powered by machine learning technologies. For details, refer to lab-specific consents in the Google Health app or the section below.

You can opt out of individual labs at any time.

How to leave Google Health Labs

You can leave individual labs at any time:

  1. Open the Google Health app .
  2. At the top right, tap your Profile picture or Initial.
  3. Tap Google Health settings and then Google Health Labs.
  4. Select the lab and tap Turn off.
  5. Confirm you want to Turn off the lab.

If you no longer want to share your Google Health data for research and development:

  1. Open the Google Health app .
  2. At the top right, tap your Profile picture or Initial.
  3. Tap Google Health settings and then Manage data and privacy and then Data shared for research and development.
  4. Read through the information in the app and then tap Turn off if you no longer want to share your data. If you turn off this feature, it won’t delete any existing data.

If you decide you want to participate in Google Health Labs again, sign up in the Health tab .

I can’t find any available labs

Some labs are only available in certain locations and languages. These labs might have requirements such as an active Google Health Premium subscription, a minimum age, or other eligibility criteria. For details on individual labs, check the section below.

If a lab is currently full, you might find a button to Join the waitlist. You need to wait until more spots open up before you can join the lab. For more information on waitlists, refer to .

What happens when a lab ends or becomes unavailable

Labs are experimental, which means they are available for a limited time and eligibility requirements might change.

The Lab has ended

If a lab comes to the end of its life cycle, it’s removed from Google Health Labs and is no longer available to eligible Fitbit users.

Identifiable data you entered as part of a lab, such as feedback or survey responses (the “Lab Data”), is automatically deleted 6 months after the lab’s end date. You may export or delete the Lab Data before that time. For more details, refer to .

Some labs work by analyzing your Google Health data from other features in the Fitbit service. Feature data analyzed by a lab but you did not directly enter into a lab, such as step count or sleep score, will not be deleted. It continues to be available in the Today page in the Google Health app.

Some labs may become available again in the future as new capabilities are added. You may have the opportunity to continue your participation at that time.

Lab eligibility

If the eligibility requirements for a lab change or you no longer meet them, you can no longer participate in the lab you previously joined. The lab appears with a prompt to “regain access” in your Labs settings.

If you correct any eligibility requirements (such as resubscribing to Google Health Premium if required) within 30 days, the lab will become available in Google Health Labs. You can then resume using it.

We won’t collect any new data during the 30-day period while the lab says “regain access,” but some processing may occur. If you correct any eligibility requirements within 30 days, we’ll resume data collection as part of the lab. Otherwise, after this period, you need to sign up and consent to the lab again if there are openings.

Why does a lab have a waitlist

Labs are open to a limited number of participants. If you’re given an option to Join the waitlist, it means the lab is full. Join the waitlist to receive a notification when more spots open up. When you receive the notification that the lab is open, be sure to sign up for the lab through the “Labs” section in the Health tab . The additional spots may be limited and you won’t be automatically added to the lab.

Delete your lab data

You may choose to delete identifiable data that you entered as part of a lab (for example, feedback or survey responses). This will delete the selected data type for all the labs you participated in.

  1. Open the Google Health app .

  5. Swipe up to review the “Labs & Research” section.

Your lab enrollment history (for example, a record of which labs you joined) will be retained unless you delete your Fitbit account and service. Fitbit may also retain lab data that doesn’t directly identify you as described in lab-specific consents. Refer to .

Unusual trends FAQs
What is Unusual trends

Important: Unusual trends is for research purposes only and is not intended to diagnose, treat, cure, mitigate, prevent, or alleviate any specific disease or condition. The information provided by Unusual trends should not be used to make medical decisions. Always consult with a qualified healthcare professional for any health concerns or before making any decisions related to your health.

Unusual trends is an experimental research capability available through Google Health Labs. It’s part of a research study designed to explore and provide awareness to the user when their physiological metrics trend away from their personal baseline. These trends are being studied to determine if they may be indicative of physical or emotional stress.

The research algorithm works with data collected by a consumer wearable device, such as a watch or tracker. It analyzes physiological metrics including heart rate variability, average heart rate during non-REM sleep, and average respiration rate during sleep. It then calculates a personal baseline for these metrics, and if the research algorithm identifies a significant change, users receive a notification prompting them to log circumstances and symptoms.

How to get started with Unusual trends

To get started with the Unusual trends research study, you must:

  • Use the Google Health app on an Android phone.
  • Use the Google Health app in English.
  • Be located in the US.
  • Be at least 22 years old.
  • Sign in to the Google Health app using a Google Account.
  • Have an offer to join the Unusual trends lab on the Health tab or Labs section of the Google Health App.

There may be additional eligibility criteria that change over time.

Opt in to the lab to start tracking your health with Unusual trends:

  1. Open the Google Health app .
  2. Go to the Health tab and scroll to the “Labs” section.
  3. Tap See all and check if you received an offer to join Unusual trends.
    1. If yes, tap Unusual trends and follow the on-screen instructions to turn on the feature.
    2. Review and accept the lab-specific research consent.
  4. Wait until you receive a notification that informs you of an unusual trend.
    • Take a survey to let us know how you feel. This feedback is essential data for our research.

Weekly, you’ll receive a notification to ask you to check in, even when there’s no unusual trend, to make sure we didn’t miss anything.

How is my data used for Unusual trends?

Specific daily health metrics collected from your Fitbit smartwatch, tracker, or Pixel smartwatch are used to identify potential unusual trends for research purposes. These metrics include Heart Rate Variability (HRV), non-REM (sleeping) heart rate, respiration rate, SpO2, and skin temperature. We analyze this data together with other Fitbit metrics, such as your sleep data, and your responses to study surveys.

Other Google Health data on activity, sleep, and stress will also be recorded during the study. This data may be used to provide additional context and improve the underlying research algorithms.

To safeguard your privacy, all personally identifiable information (PII) is removed from your data, and each participant is assigned a unique study ID. Your data is then stored on secure backend servers with access restricted to authorized personnel. Only de-identified data is used for analysis, ensuring your privacy is protected throughout the study.

Our research focus is on analyzing trends and patterns in the de-identified health data to improve our algorithms and provide valuable insights.

How to provide feedback for Unusual trends

Your feedback is essential for this research and to enhance the Unusual trends experience for all users. You can contribute in 2 ways:

Feedback on Positive Detections

  • If Unusual trends detects a potential unusual trend, a dedicated card will appear on your Today tab. This card includes a button to access a brief survey. This card and its associated survey are persistent, available at any time, and don’t go away after the survey has been completed.
  • We encourage you to complete this survey whenever your condition or symptoms change. This provides us valuable insights into the evolution of your health.

Feedback on General Well-being

  • Even when Unusual trends doesn’t detect any unusual trends, you can still access the feedback card to let us know how you’re feeling. This helps us clear out any false negative cases.
  • We provide a weekly notification to remind you to check in and provide feedback, even when no detections have occurred.

When you provide feedback through these methods, you help refine the Unusual trend’s accuracy and effectiveness.

Limitations of Unusual trends

As Unusual trends is currently an experimental research capability, it’s important to understand its limitations. It is not validated for any specific health outcome or condition. However, previous studies have shown that the algorithm is typically associated with events that cause physical or emotional stress, such as:

  • Respiratory illness
  • Travel
  • Alcohol consumption

We’re actively working to refine the research algorithm and gain a deeper understanding of the complex relationship between health metrics and potential health events.

Therefore, you may occasionally receive a positive detection notification that doesn’t align with your perceived physical or emotional state. The algorithm may fail to identify trends even when you’re experiencing stress or other changes. Do not rely on Unusual trends for any health assessment.

We appreciate your patience and understanding as we conduct this research to continue to improve Unusual trends’ performance and accuracy. Your feedback is crucial in helping us address these limitations and enhance the system’s effectiveness.

How to turn off Unusual trends
  1. Open the Google Health app .
  2. At the top right, tap your Profile picture or Initial.
  3. Tap Settings and then Labs and then Unusual trends.
  4. Tap Turn off.
  5. Confirm you want to turn off Unusual trends.

If you want to participate again in the future, follow the instructions in .

Unusual trends sent a notification but no metrics are out of range on the dashboard

Unusual trends research algorithm tracks a combination of your metrics over several days, while the Health Metrics Dashboard mainly shows individual metrics from the last day. Because they use different algorithms and offer different ways of looking at your data, Unusual trends notifications may not always match your Health Metrics Dashboard.

Unusual trends sent a notification but I feel perfectly fine

The Unusual trends research algorithm may be detecting patterns in your metrics that aren’t necessarily associated with symptoms or how you feel. Part of this research is to gain a better understanding of how these patterns are associated with different behaviors and circumstances, with the goal of increasing awareness. Receiving a notification when you feel fine is possible and provides useful data for the study.

Why send notifications if Unusual trends is just a research feature

The main purpose of the notification is to prompt you for timely feedback through the survey when our research algorithm has identified a pattern in your physiological metrics that differs from your baseline. It’s essential for our research to get your input at the specific time a pattern is flagged. It helps us learn whether the patterns identified by the algorithm are related to how users actually feel or experience things.

Your feedback is crucial to evaluate and improve this experimental technology.

Who should I contact if I have more questions

Our research lead, Anthony Faranesh, PhD, can answer any questions about this Lab.

Mobile:

  • 1-415-610-4848‬ Mondays to Fridays (9:00–5:00 PM Pacific TIme)
  • 1-877-623-4997 (24 hours)

Email: gtrial@google.com

Always consult your healthcare provider for medical decisions. The notifications created in this study are not medical advice or diagnoses. Your healthcare practitioner is best equipped to provide personalized medical advice.

Get Care Now Lab
What is the Get Care Now Lab?

Get Care Now Lab is a research project designed to assess artificial intelligence (AI) system’s performance in the real world. In this Lab, you will have the opportunity to get a consultation, at no cost, with a virtual care provider from Doctor On Demand by Included Health through a video call. Participants are randomly assigned to either have a chat with an AI agent about their symptoms before their virtual care visit or go directly to their virtual consultation. The study uses generative AI to gather your health history and symptoms, providing a summary for both you and your clinician to help prepare for your visit.

The AI system used in this Lab is not intended to:

  • Diagnose or treat any disease or condition.
  • Provide medical advice or be used for self-diagnosis.
  • Mitigate or prevent any disease or condition
  • Be used as a substitute for professional medical advice
  • Provide guidance to users to make specific changes to their medication or treatment plans

Always consult with a healthcare professional for any health concerns. Results may be inaccurate and should not be used to make decisions about your health.

IF YOU BELIEVE YOU ARE EXPERIENCING A MEDICAL EMERGENCY, CALL YOUR LOCAL EMERGENCY SERVICES IMMEDIATELY. DO NOT RELY ON THIS TOOL FOR URGENT HEALTH CONCERNS.

How do I get started with Get Care Now Lab?

To be eligible to participate, you must:

  • Be 21 years of age or older.
  • Reside in the United States.
  • Be seeking a virtual urgent care consultation for your own personal health issues (not for a family member or child).
  • Review and accept the lab-specificinformed consent form within the Google Health app.
  • Be a Google Health app user, signed in with a Google account on an Android smartphone.
  • Use the Google Health app in English.
  • Satisfy the study enrichment criteria.
Opt into Get Care Now Lab

Important: This study is available for the first 5,000 eligible users who sign up and complete the end-to-end flow. If this lab is already full, you can try a few days later as spots might open up.

How to enroll*:

  1. From the Google Health app’s Health tab , find the “Google Health Labs” section.

    Tap See all and check for an offer to enroll in the lab.

    • If you see Get Care Now Lab, tap the lab and follow the on-screen instructions to turn on the feature.
    • If you don’t see Get Care Now Lab, it is not yet available on your account.

  2. Review, accept, and submit the lab-specific consent and questionnaire.

How does the Get Care Now lab work?

Once you enroll, you will be randomly assigned to one of two groups:

  1. Active Group: You will start a chat with an AI agent about your symptoms within the Google Health Labs section of your app. Afterward, you will proceed to your virtual visit with a clinician from Doctor On Demand by Included Health.
  2. Control Group: You will go directly to your virtual consultation with the clinician without starting a chat with an AI agent.

In both groups, a licensed clinician is solely responsible for your medical care, including any diagnosis, treatment, or management plans.

*Participants must meet Labs minimum requirements to begin the enrollment process.

When should I use the Get Care Now Lab?

Get Care Now lab is designed as a research tool to help you explore and become more aware of potential topics your clinician may discuss with you, such as reasons and potential next steps related to the symptoms you’re experiencing. You can use it when you are seeking a virtual urgent care consultation for your own personal health issues (not for a family member or child).

Remember, this is for research purposes only and the results are not a diagnosis. For more information, see the limitations below.

What are the limitations of the Get Care Now lab?

This AI system is an experimental research tool and has important limitations:

  • Informational Only: All information provided by the AI is for research purposes and is not a substitute for professional medical advice.
  • Potential Inaccuracy: Generative AI can sometimes produce incomplete or clinically inaccurate information
  • Scope: The AI is designed for common urgent care symptoms (like respiratory, gastrointestinal, or skin issues) and is not equipped to handle medical emergencies or complex mental health crises.

If you’re experiencing a medical emergency, contact emergency services. Do not rely on this tool.

How is my Get Care Now Lab data used?

Your data is used for research and development to evaluate large language models (LLM) and to improve the underlying language models’ performance. This includes:

  • User inputted conversation data: User-inputted conversation data, like symptoms, help evaluate the model’s ability to ask and answer questions.
  • User Profile Data: User profile (e.g., Age, Sex) is used to verify study participation and is used to provide personalized model responses.
  • Google Health Data: Wearable data may be analyzed alongside user symptoms to explore correlations and validate machine learning algorithms, but this data is not used to provide individual health insights or assessments within this lab.
  • Survey Responses & AI Interactions: Feedback, questions, and healthcare provider notes help researchers understand user experience, utility, and the technical performance of the AI’s responses within the research context.

Your data helps with research and development of Google products.

Data is de-identified, but complete anonymity is not guaranteed. The handling, use, and sharing of all your study data, including health details you choose to share, such as symptoms or diagnoses from your healthcare providers, are governed by the lab-specific Informed Consent Form (ICF).

How is my health data kept secure?

Data collected during this research study is handled according to the security and privacy protocols outlined in the lab-specific Informed Consent Form (ICF).

How do I provide feedback for the Get Care Now lab?

After you complete the consultation, you’ll have the opportunity to complete a brief survey to share your feedback. You will also have an opportunity to provide feedback for the 2-3 weeks after your visit where we will ask for information related to the resolution of your symptoms. Some participants will be offered the opportunity to participate in an optional User Experience interview to provide additional feedback of their experience with the lab. Your feedback will help us improve this feature.

Where can I find more detailed information about how my data is handled in this study?

For comprehensive details regarding how your data will be used, stored, and protected in the Get Care Now lab, please carefully review the lab-specific Informed Consent Form (ICF) that you accepted when you opted into the study. This consent form contains important information about:

  • The types of data being collected, such as personal data, AI interactions, Google Health data, survey responses, and user profile.
  • How this data will be used for research and development, including the training of AI models.
  • Data de-identification and potential data sharing.
  • Your rights and responsibilities as a participant in this research study.

By reviewing the consent, you’ll gain a thorough understanding of how your information will be used to contribute to this important research on generative AI and symptom understanding.

Will I be compensated for my participation in this study

Yes, participants will receive incentives for completing the study procedures, as detailed in your Informed Consent Form (ICF).

Can I leave the study at any time?

Yes, your participation is completely voluntary. You can choose to withdraw from the study at any time through the settings in your app.

To leave the Get Care Now Lab:

  1. Open the Google Health app .
  2. At the top right, tap your Profile picture or Initial.
  3. Tap Google Health settings and then Labs and then Get Care Now Lab.
  4. Tap Turn off.
  5. Confirm that you want to exit the lab.
Who should I contact if I have more questions

Our research team can answer any questions about this Lab. Email: get-care-now-study@google.com

Always consult your healthcare provider for medical decisions. The responses and resulting set of responses for symptoms created in this study are not medical advice or diagnoses. Your healthcare practitioner is best equipped to provide personalized medical advice based on your complete medical history.

Plan for Care Lab
What is the Plan for Care Lab

Plan for Care Lab is a new experimental capability in Labs for research-use only. When trying out this lab, users will be randomly assigned to a different set of instructions. It uses generative artificial intelligence (AI) to guide users through a series of symptom-related questions (depending on the instruction that is assigned) and provides the user with a set of possible associated reasons for symptoms as well as an estimation of urgency. The lab can also brainstorm with the user about upcoming visits and help users prepare.

The lab is not intended to:

  • Diagnose
  • Treat or cure
  • Mitigate or prevent any disease or condition
  • Be used as a substitute for professional medical advice
  • Provide guidance to users to make specific changes to their medication or treatment plans

Always consult with a healthcare professional for any health concerns. Results may be inaccurate and should not be used to make decisions about your health.

IF YOU BELIEVE YOU ARE EXPERIENCING A MEDICAL EMERGENCY, CALL YOUR LOCAL EMERGENCY SERVICES IMMEDIATELY. DO NOT RELY ON THIS TOOL FOR URGENT HEALTH CONCERNS.

When should I use the Plan for Care Lab?

Plan for Care lab is designed as a research tool to help you explore and become more aware of potential reasons related to the symptoms you’re experiencing or have experienced and help you prepare for upcoming doctor visits. You can use it when you notice new, changing, or chronic symptoms, and want to see a range of possibilities that might be associated with them. You can also use it when you have an upcoming visit you want to plan for.

Remember, this is for research purposes only and the results are not a diagnosis. For more information, see the limitations below.

What are the limitations of the Plan for Care lab?

This lab is an experimental research tool using generative AI. It has significant limitations.

  • Plan for Care lab uses generative AI, which may sometimes lead to incomplete, out-of-date, or clinically inaccurate or misleading information. It is not a source of verified medical information.
  • Plan for Care lab lets you use open free-text to respond to symptom questions. However, diverging from the structured conversation or attempting to respond back with questions of your own may not result in a detailed response.
  • Misinterpretation of your input and responses is a potential limitation of this tool. The tool is designed for exploring general symptom patterns. It is not equipped to interpret complex medical data, provide specialized advice, for instance on drug interactions, or respond appropriately to all types of user input, especially those related to severe distress or mental health crises.
  • The information provided by the Plan for Care Lab is for research and informational purposes only and does not constitute medical advice or diagnosis. The LLM does not have medical expertise and cannot understand your full health context. Your healthcare practitioner is best equipped to provide personalized medical advice based on your complete medical history.

If you’re experiencing a medical emergency, contact emergency services. Do not rely on this tool.

  • Google Health Data: Wearable data may be analyzed alongside user symptoms to explore correlations and validate machine learning algorithms, but this data is not used to provide individual health insights or assessments within this lab.
  • Survey Responses & AI Interactions: Feedback, questions, and healthcare provider notes help researchers understand user experience, utility, and the technical performance of the AI’s responses within the research context.

Your data helps with research and development of Google products.

Hypertension Study Lab (Google Pixel Watch 3)
What is the Hypertension Lab

The Hypertension Lab is a research study designed to help us learn how to use Pixel Watch data to identify early signs of Hypertension. The goal is to advance research that could one day help users take proactive steps toward better heart health.

This study will proceed in 2 parts:

  1. We’ll recruit up to 10,000 eligible participants to wear their Google Pixel Watch 3 as they normally would for 180 days.
  2. A subset of those participants will be asked to participate in an ABPM cuff study. We’ll mail out a blood pressure cuff, called an Ambulatory Blood Pressure Monitoring (ABPM) device, to wear for 24 hours. If a user is selected as a participant and agrees to participate, we’ll provide detailed instructions on how to use and return, and other study information.
Will the study provide me with medical advice

No, the information from this study is for research purposes only and will not provide you with any medical advice, analysis, or feedback on your health. Always consult with a healthcare professional for any health concerns.

  • Be 22 years of age or older
  • Live in the United States
  • Use the Google Health app in English
  • Have a Pixel Watch 3
    • Pixel Watch 1, Pixel Watch 2, and Pixel Watch 4 are not eligible
  • Be able to fill in the questionnaire

Software requirements:

  • Pixel Watch Software Version: BP3A.250905.014 or later
    • Tip: To check, go to Settings and then About and then Versions and then Build number
  • Google Health app on your Pixel Watch: Version 3.45 or later
  • Google Health app: Version 4.55 or later
