How do I respond to messages with my Fitbit device?

Use quick replies to send customized responses to text messages and messages from certain apps with Fitbit Charge 3, Fitbit Charge 4, Fitbit Charge 5, Fitbit Charge 6, Fitbit Inspire 3, Fitbit Luxe, Fitbit Sense series, or Fitbit Versa series.

Important: Some users may experience a transcription error when attempting to send Alexa voice replies on Versa 2, Versa 3, Versa 4, Sense, and Sense 2. Our team is aware of this issue and working towards a fix.

This feature is currently available on devices paired to an Android phone. Devices paired to an iPhone can respond to Google Health app notifications, such as messages, cheers, taunts, and friend requests.

How do I set up quick replies from my Fitbit device?

Quick replies are automatically turned on for any supported apps that send notifications from your phone to your Fitbit device. For more information, check Change phone notifications on my Fitbit device

To receive and respond to messages from your device, your phone must be nearby with Bluetooth turned on and the Google Health app running in the background. To use the microphone to respond to messages in Sense, Sense 2, Versa 2, Versa 3, or Versa 4, in the Settings app , make sure the Microphone setting is turned on.

How do I use quick replies on my Fitbit device?

When you receive a notification from your phone, your device vibrates. To respond with a quick reply:

Charge 5, Charge 6, Google Pixel Watch, Google Pixel Watch 2, Inspire 3, and Luxe
  1. Tap the notification on your tracker to open it. To check recent messages, swipe right or left on the Notifications app , then swipe up.
  2. Choose how to reply to the message:
    • Tap the text icon to respond to the message from a list of quick replies.
    • Tap the emoji icon to respond to the message with an emoji.

For Google Pixel Watch quick replies, refer to Make and receive phone calls and SMS texts on Pixel Watch.

Sense, Sense 2, Versa 3, and Versa 4
  1. Tap the notification on your watch. To check recent messages, swipe down from the screen.
  2. Choose how to reply to the message:
    • Tap the microphone icon to respond to the message using voice-to-text. To change the language recognized by the microphone, tap Language. After you speak your reply, tap Send, or tap Retry to try again.
      • On Sense and Versa 3, if you notice a mistake after you send the message, tap Undo within 3 seconds to cancel the message.
    • Tap the text icon to respond to a message from a list of quick replies.
    • Tap the emoji icon to respond to the message with an emoji.
All other devices
  1. Tap the notification on your device. To check recent notifications, swipe down from the top of the screen.
  2. Tap Reply or Replies. If you don’t have an option to reply to the message, quick replies aren’t available for the app that sent the notification.
  3. Choose a text reply from the list of quick replies or tap the emoji icon to choose an emoji. Tap More replies or More emojis to check additional options.
  4. On Versa 2, tap the microphone icon and say your message. If the message is correct, tap Send, or tap Retry to try again. If you notice a mistake after you send the message, tap Undo within 3 seconds to cancel the message.
    • To change the language recognized by the microphone, tap the 3 dots icon next to Languages and choose a different language.
How do I customize the quick replies on my Fitbit device?

Each app has a list of 5 default text quick replies. To change the quick replies:

  1. Open the Google Health app .
  2. At the top left, tap Connections and then your device.
  3. Tap Notifications and then Quick replies and then the app you want to change the quick replies for.
    • To change the default quick replies for all apps, tap Custom replies.
  4. Tap the reply you want to change and enter the text you want to use instead. Replies are limited to 60 characters. Tap Save.
  5. Tap the back arrow to return to the app list.
  6. Sync your device. The next time you receive a message notification from that app, your new reply is included in the list of quick replies on your device.
Which apps let me send quick replies from my Fitbit device?

Apps that allow you to reply to a message directly from the notification on your Android phone also support quick replies on your Fitbit device. This includes, but isn’t limited to, apps such as:

  • X (formerly Twitter)

Note that devices paired to an iPhone can only respond to Google Health app notifications.

What are the reminders on my Fitbit device

Receive reminders on your Fitbit device that encourage healthy behaviors.

Important: Reminders are turned off while you’re asleep.

Reminders to move

What’s a Fitbit reminder to move?

Stay active during the day with an hourly activity goal and reminders to move.

A reminder to move is a notification that cues you to walk at least 250 steps per hour to help you meet your hourly activity goal. If you haven’t walked 250 steps, the reminder appears on your device at 10 minutes before the hour (for example, at 10:50 a.m.) and causes your device to vibrate.

What’s my hourly activity goal on my Fitbit device?

To start, your hourly activity goal is to take at least 250 steps per hour (which equals a few minutes of walking) from 9:00 a.m. - 6:00 p.m., 7 days a week. You can adjust the hours that you track your goal and receive reminders to move.

Note that activities that don’t include steps, such as spinning, won’t count toward your goal. If you miss your goal, you can’t make it up by taking extra steps the next hour.

To change your goal, see Track your health and fitness goals with Google Health.

Why do I have an hourly activity goal on my Fitbit device?

Research shows that sitting for long periods of time is linked with a higher risk of health issues, including obesity, increased blood pressure, high blood sugar, and abnormal cholesterol levels (source). Even if you meet daily exercise guidelines, extended sitting can impact your health (source). Moving a few minutes every hour can help to reduce the negative effects of sitting (source).

How do I check my hourly activity chart?
Google Health app

Fitness tab

  1. Open the Google Health app and tap the Fitness tab .
  2. Scroll to “Hourly Activity”.
  3. Tap on the graph to view a breakdown of your hourly activity.

Today tab

  1. Open the Google Health app .
  2. On the Today tab , in your dashboard, tap Hourly activity to view a breakdown of your hourly activity.
  3. If the Hourly activity tile is not present:
    1. On the Today tab , tap Edit .
    2. Tap on an empty tile or a tile that you want to replace.
    3. On the corner of the “Hourly activity” tile, tap Add .
How do I see how many days I met my hourly activity goal?
Google Health app
  1. Open the Google Health app and tap the Fitness tab .
  2. Scroll to and tap Hourly Activity.
Fitbit devices
  1. From the clock screen, swipe up to find your Exercise days or on some devices open Google Health .
  2. On the Hourly Activity tile , see how many steps you took this hour.
  3. Swipe to see how many hours you met your goal today.
Google Pixel Watch series
  1. Press the crown, swipe up to the Google Health app , and tap the app to open it.
  2. Swipe to the Hourly Activity card and see how many hours you met your goal today.
  3. Tap the card for more details.
Can I change when I receive reminders to move on my Fitbit device?

To change when you receive reminders to move, change the hours or days of the week that you track your hourly activity goal (for example, 10:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. on weekdays).

To change your goal, see Track your health and fitness goals with Google Health.

How do I turn reminders to move on or off on my Fitbit device?

On most devices, you can turn off notifications so you temporarily don’t get reminders to move. For instructions, check Change phone notifications on my Fitbit device.

To permanently turn reminders to move off:

Google Health app
  1. At the top left, tap Connections and then your device
  2. Tap Google Health reminders & alerts and then Reminders to move.
  3. Tap Get reminders to turn it on or off.

Note: Google Pixel Watch 4 will have reminders to move off by default.

Why didn’t my Fitbit device alert me?

Your Fitbit device vibrates to alert you at various times, including if you set an alarm, when you hit your step goal, or if you haven’t met your hourly activity goal.

If your device didn’t alert you:

  • Make sure you successfully set an alarm. For more information, see How do I manage alarms on my Fitbit device?
  • Make sure Do Not Disturb and Sleep Mode are turned off on your Fitbit device. For more information, see How do I navigate my Fitbit device?
  • On Fitbit Charge 3 and Fitbit Charge 4, turn on Exercise alerts to receive notifications about your workout in the Exercise app while do not disturb is on. Open the Settings app Do Not DisturbExercise alerts.
  • On Fitbit Inspire, Fitbit Inspire HR, and Fitbit Inspire 2, make sure that notifications are turned on under quick settings. For more information, see How do I navigate my Fitbit device?
  • If device lock is active on your Fitbit device, make sure you entered your PIN code recently to unlock your device.
  • For health and wellness reminders, make sure your phone is within 30 feet of your Fitbit device.

Note that on Fitbit Versa, Fitbit Versa Lite Edition, and Fitbit Versa 2, alarms don’t alert you if your battery is below 8%.

If you correctly set the alarm or aren’t receiving other alerts, test your device’s vibration motor:

Ace and Alta series

Connect the device to the charging cable and press the button. The button is on the end of the charging cable that you plug into a USB port. For more information, see How do I charge my Fitbit device?

Ace 2, Ace 3, Charge series, Flex 2, Inspire series, Luxe, Sense series, Versa 3, and Versa 4

Connect the device to the charging cable. For more information, see How do I charge my Fitbit device?

Blaze, Versa, Versa Lite Edition, and Versa 2
  1. Open Timer and choose the stopwatch.
  2. Tap the play icon to start. Your device should vibrate.

If you still have trouble, contact Customer Support.

Payments

Google Fitbit Air HSA/FSA Eligibility

Important: This article applies to US customers only, for devices purchased June 15, 2026 and later.

Google Fitbit Air (excluding special editions) is HSA and FSA eligible under many health plans to qualifying customers. That means you may be able to use your Health Savings Account (HSA) or Flexible Spending Account (FSA) to cover the cost of the device, if you qualify, depending on the requirements of your health plan administrator.

Always check plan eligibility

  • Before purchasing, confirm with your plan administrator if your purchase of Google Fitbit Air (excluding special editions) is covered. Eligibility and reimbursement procedures vary by HSA/FSA plan and administrator.
  • Google cannot guarantee that Google Fitbit Air will be eligible for reimbursement from your FSA or HSA. Whether or not an expense may be reimbursed from your FSA or HSA depends on your specific circumstances, such as your healthcare plan.
  • Your health plan administrator may ask you to provide additional documentation.

If eligible, use HSA/FSA funds to buy Google Fitbit Air [Excluding Special Editions]

After confirming that your administrator will cover your purchase of Google Fitbit Air, you can pay for Google Fitbit Air directly with an HSA or FSA card at certain retailers. If the retailer doesn’t accept HSA/FSA cards, you can pay for the device yourself, then submit the receipt to your health plan administrator for reimbursement.

Get reimbursed from your HSA/FSA (Google Store)

For Google Store and other retailers that don’t accept payment with HSA/FSA cards, you may be eligible to get reimbursed for your Google Fitbit Air purchase:

  1. Buy Google Fitbit Air: Buy the device from the Google Store or an authorized retailer using a standard payment method (for example, credit card or debit card).
  2. Keep your receipt: Make sure to save the itemized receipt for your purchase. This receipt will serve as proof of purchase for your HSA/FSA administrator. For purchases from Google Store, you will receive an email confirmation of your receipt.
  3. Submit for reimbursement: Send your receipt and any other required documentation to your HSA/FSA plan administrator for reimbursement. Before purchasing, always check with your plan administrator for specific submission guidelines and forms, as the process can vary by plan.
Pay with your HSA/FSA card at qualifying retailers
  1. Purchase Google Fitbit Air: Buy your device from the authorized retailer using the HSA or FSA card provided by your plan administrator.
  2. Keep your receipt: Make sure to save the itemized receipt for your purchase. This receipt will serve as proof of purchase for your HSA/FSA administrator.
  3. Submit documentation: If your administrator requires it, submit your receipt to your HSA/FSA plan administrator as proof that your purchase was for a qualified medical expense.

How do I use iPASS with my Fitbit device?

Add a new iPASS card or your iPASS co-branded credit card to Fitbit Charge 3, Fitbit Charge 4, Fitbit Charge 5, Fitbit Charge 6, Fitbit Sense series, and Fitbit Versa series*. Make payments right from your device anywhere iPASS is supported.

*This feature isn’t available on Fitbit Versa Lite Edition.

Important: To use iPASS with Google Wallet, please update to the latest version of the Google Health app.

Where is iPASS used?

iPASS is a Taiwanese e-wallet that can be used in public transport and retail stores. To determine if iPASS can be used, look for the symbol below on the payment or transit terminal:

For more information on iPASS, refer to iPASS’s overview. For information on where iPASS can be used for transit and Micro payment or eMoney, refer to iPASS’s list of stores.

How do I add a virtual iPASS card to my Fitbit device?
  1. Open the Google Health app .
  2. At the top left, tap Connections and then your device.
  3. Tap Google and then Wallet and then Continue.
  4. If you haven’t already done so, follow the on-screen instructions to set a 4-digit PIN code for your device.
  5. Tap iPASS to add a virtual iPASS card to your device. Follow the on-screen instructions and add the card to your Google Wallet.

Tip: iPASS is only listed as an option if your location is set to Taiwan.

How many iPASS cards can I have in my Google Wallet and on my device?

You can add up to 6 iPASS cards to your Google Wallet, one of which can be a virtual iPASS card. The others must be co-branded credit cards.

Only your default iPASS card will be shown on your Fitbit device. You can change your default card setting in the Google Health app.

How do I pay for transit or other items using my iPASS card on my Fitbit device?

After adding a transit card to your Wallet, hold your wrist near the iPASS reader (within 6 centimeters) until you feel your Fitbit device vibrate. Note that you don’t need to pull up the iPASS card art in the Payments screen or enter your PIN on your Fitbit device to pay with your iPASS card.

How do I change the default iPASS card on my Fitbit device?

When you hold your wrist to the transit reader, it automatically pulls funds from your default iPASS card. To change your default card if you have more than one iPASS card:

  1. Open the Google Health app .
  2. At the top left, tap Connections and then your device.
  3. Tap Google and then Wallet and then Continue.
  4. Tap your default iPASS card.
  5. Tap Make default for iPass and then Make default to set as your default card.
How do I add value to my iPASS card?

After adding a virtual iPASS card to your Fitbit device, place your device on the ticket vending machine terminal. Follow the instructions on the machine to add value to your virtual card.

An iPASS co-branded credit card automatically reloads when you tap it to an iPASS reader and the card has insufficient funds.

How do I add my iPASS co-branded credit card to my Google Wallet?
  1. Open the Google Health app .
  2. At the top left, tap Connections and then your device.
  3. Tap Google and then Wallet and then Continue.
  4. Tap Credit or debit. Or, add the card you want to use.
  5. Follow the on-screen instructions and add the card to Google Wallet.

Tip: If your co-branded credit card is part of the Google Wallet on the Fitbit iPASS program, follow the steps in What should I know about using my Fitbit device to make contactless payments? to add your card to Google Wallet. If your bank requires additional verification, choose the SMS option to verify your card. After accepting the terms and conditions, your iPASS card is automatically added.

I added my co-branded credit card, but my iPASS card was not added—what should I do?

When you add your co-branded credit card to Google Wallet, your bank may require additional verification. Choose the SMS option to verify your card and add your iPASS card. If you instead verified your card through customer support, contact your bank for further instructions.

If you still aren’t able to add your iPASS card, remove your co-branded credit card from your Google Wallet in the Google Health app and try adding it again.

Do I need to have my phone nearby to use my iPASS card?

You don’t need to have your phone nearby to use any of the cards in your Google Wallet. After you set up your cards, you can make payments from your Fitbit device and leave your phone at home.

Where can I check the current balance left on my iPASS card?
  1. Open the Google Health app .
  2. At the top left, tap Connections and then your device.
  3. Tap Google and then Wallet and then Continue. The balance of your default card is shown.
  4. If you have more than one card, tap the default card. The balance of your other cards is shown.

Tip: An iPASS co-branded credit card automatically reloads when you tap it to a iPASS reader and the card has insufficient funds.

How do I transfer the remaining balance from my iPASS card?
  1. Register your iPASS card at i-pass.com.tw/Miss or from within the Google Health app. For more information, refer to
  2. Contact iPASS Customer Support to transfer your remaining balance.
How do I delete an iPASS card from my Fitbit device?
  1. If you have remaining balance on your iPASS card, transfer the balance.
  2. Open the Google Health app .
  3. At the top left, tap Connections and then your device.
  4. Tap the Google and then Wallet and then Continue .
  5. Tap your iPASS card.
  6. Swipe or scroll to the bottom of the page and tap Remove Google Wallet card from Fitbit and then Remove.
How do I suspend or delete an iPASS co-branded credit card from my Fitbit device?
  1. Open the Google Health app .
  2. At the top left, tap Connections and then your device.
  3. Tap Google and then Wallet and then Continue.
  4. Tap your card.
  5. Swipe or scroll to the bottom of the page and select Remove from device.

When you suspend a card, your iPASS balance will still be available to use on your Fitbit device, but the card won’t auto-reload. You can unsuspend it at any time from the Google Health app.

When you remove a card, it cannot be used for purchases or transit from your Fitbit device until it’s re-added from the Google Wallet app.

How do I register my iPASS card?

Register your iPASS card to ensure your balance can be retrieved through iPASS customer support if your Fitbit device is lost or erased.

  1. Open the Google Health app .
  2. At the top left, tap Connections and then your device.
  3. Tap the Google and then Wallet and then Continue.
  4. Tap your card.
  5. Tap Register iPASS, which directs you to i-pass.com.tw/Miss.
What happens when my co-branded iPASS card expires?

If you receive a replacement card for your co-branded credit card, the new information is updated automatically in your Google Wallet.

I lost my Fitbit device. What should I do?

If you lost your device, you can remove the card you added to the device using the instructions in

I lost my phone and my Fitbit device. What should I do?

If you lost both devices, you can log into Google Wallet to deactivate the cards or passes.

  1. Open the Google Health app .
  2. At the top left, tap Connections and then your device.
  3. Tap Google and then Wallet and then Continue.
  4. Tap the cards or passes you want to delete.
  5. Tap Details and then Remove payment method or Remove Pass.
I want to give my Fitbit device to someone else. What should I do?

Register your iPASS card to ensure your remaining balance can be transferred through iPASS customer support. For more information, refer to How do I register my iPASS card?

After you register your card, factory reset your device to erase all personal data. For instructions, refer to How do I erase my Fitbit device?

Tip: A factory reset will remove the iPASS card from your device. Any funds remaining on an unregistered iPASS card (未記名卡) will be lost when you remove the card. The only way to retrieve the remaining balance is if you registered your card.

Why isn’t iPASS listed as an option in the Google Health app?

The transit options listed in your Google Wallet are based on your location. To add an iPASS card, you must set your Google Health account location to Taiwan or your phone’s device region must be set to Taiwan:

  1. Open the Google Health app .
  2. At the top right, tap your Profile picture or Initial.
  3. Tap Google Health settingsDate, time & unitsLocation.
  4. Set your location to Taiwan.
How do I get help with iPass on my Fitbit device?

If you need help with your iPass account, contact iPass directly. Visit the iPass website for contact information: i-pass.com.tw.

How do I use Suica on my Fitbit device?

Add Suica to your Fitbit device to pay for transit and goods anywhere Suica is accepted.

Where is Suica used?

Suica is a prepaid e-money card issued by Japan Railway East (JR East). It’s used to pay for transit and for goods at certain vending machines, convenience stores, coin lockers, and many more retail stores. Stores that accept Suica typically display an e-money symbol. For more information on where Suica is accepted, refer to jreast.co.jp.

Which Fitbit devices are compatible with Suica?

Google Pixel Watch Series, Fitbit Charge 4, Fitbit Charge 5, Fitbit Charge 6, Fitbit Sense, Fitbit Sense 2, Fitbit Versa 3, and Fitbit Versa 4 are compatible with Suica. To use Suica:

Charge 4

Screenshot: Sticker with an image of a Suica card on it and a QR code

Note that not all Charge 4 trackers are compatible with Suica.

Charge 5, Charge 6, Sense, Sense 2, Versa 3, and Versa 4
  • Sense and Versa 3 must be running Fitbit OS 5.2 or higher. For more information on updating your watch, refer to How do I update my Fitbit device?
  • Use the latest version of the Google Health app.
How do I set up Suica on my Fitbit device?
  1. Open the Google Health app .
  2. At the top left, tap Connections and then your device.
  3. Tap GoogleWallet.
  4. Follow the on-screen instructions to set a 4-digit PIN code for your device if you haven’t already done so.
  5. Tap Suica, and follow the on-screen instructions to add Suica to your Google Wallet.
    • As part of the initial Suica setup, you’re asked to use Google Wallet to add value to Suica. For more information on Google Wallet, refer to support.google.com.

Note that if you don’t refer to the Suica tile isn’t listed in your Google Wallet, your device isn’t compatible with Suica. For more information, refer to Which Fitbit devices are compatible with Suica?

How do I pay for transit or goods with Suica on my Fitbit device?

After you add Suica to your Wallet, hold your Fitbit device near an automated gate, bus on-board reader, or the Suica reader to pay for transit or goods. Note that you don’t need to wake your Fitbit device’s screen or enter your PIN to pay with Suica, but your device must be turned on.

When you use Suica on your Fitbit device for transit, make sure Suica has sufficient funds and your device is charged before beginning your trip.

How do I check the current balance of Suica on my Fitbit device?
Google Health app
  1. Open the Google Health app .
  2. At the top left, tap Connections and then your device.
  3. Tap GoogleWallet.
  4. Follow the on-screen instructions.
  5. Your current balance is listed under Suica in the Instant Access section.
On-device
Charge 4
  1. Press and hold the button on Charge 4 for 2 seconds.
  2. If prompted, enter your 4-digit tracker PIN code. Your default card appears on the screen.
  3. If Suica isn’t your default card, tap to find it. Your current balance is listed under Suica.
Google Pixel Watch
  1. Tap the Wallet tile on your watch.
  2. Tap Suica.
  3. Swipe down.
  4. Tap Details.
Sense, Sense 2, Versa 3, and Versa 4
  1. Open the Wallet app on your watch.
  2. If prompted, enter your 4-digit watch PIN code. Your default card appears on the screen.
  3. If Suica isn’t your default card, tap to find it. Your current balance is listed under Suica.
Charge 5 and Charge 6
  1. Swipe down from the clock face and tap Payments.
  2. If prompted, enter your 4-digit tracker PIN code. Your default card appears on the screen.
  3. If Suica isn’t your default card, swipe up to find it. Your current balance is listed under Suica.
How do I get my SUICA top-up receipt?

Please go to this link to apply for a top-up receipt.

How do I add funds to Suica on my Fitbit device?
  1. Open the Google Health app .
  2. At the top left, tap Connections and then your device.
  3. Tap GoogleWallet.
  4. Tap SuicaAdd Money.
  5. Follow the on-screen instructions to add value to Suica using Google Wallet.

Note that auto-charge isn’t available for Suica on your Fitbit device.

If you prefer to use cash to add funds to Suica, use a JR East tray-type ticket machine or ask the cashier at a convenience store that accepts Suica.

How do I update my personal information for Suica in the Google Health app?
  1. Open the Google Health app .
  2. At the top left, tap Connections and then your device.
  3. Tap GoogleWallet.
  4. Tap SuicaYour Info.
  5. Update your information, and then tap Save.

Note that if you remove Suica and set up a new card, your personal information is saved from the first card. To update your personal information, follow the instructions above after you set up your new card.

How do I open and download my Suica transaction history in the Google Health app?
  1. Open the Google Health app .
  2. At the top left, tap Connections and then your device.
  3. Tap GoogleWallet.
  4. Tap SuicaActivity. Check your recent transactions, including transit rides, purchases and top-ups.
  5. To receive an email with your transaction history, tap the email icon Send.

Transactions can take 24 hours to appear in your transaction history in the Google Health app.

Note that the transaction history for Suica on your Fitbit device is only available in the Google Health app for the registered emails. You won’t encounter these transactions in the mobile Suica app.

How do I remove Suica from my Fitbit device?
  1. Open the Google Health app .
  2. At the top left, tap Connections and then your device.
  3. Tap GoogleWallet.
  4. Tap SuicaDelete from device.
    • If you want a refund for your balance, tap Refund and Remove. Note the following:
      • To receive a refund, your card must have a balance of at least ¥221.
      • You must fill out a refund application in the Google Health app. The refund application including your bank information is submitted to JR East.
      • You must have a Japanese bank account to receive your refund.
      • Suica charges a ¥220 removal fee, which is deducted from your refund.
    • If you don’t want a refund, tap Remove Without a Refund. Suica is removed from your Fitbit device, but your remaining balance isn’t refunded to your bank account.
How do I suspend Suica on my Fitbit device?
  1. Open the Google Health app .
  2. At the top left, tap Connections and then your device.
  3. Tap GoogleWallet.
  4. Tap SuicaDeactivate.

When Suica is suspended, your Fitbit device isn’t recognized by the automated gate, bus on-board reader, or Suica reader. To resume functionality, tap Resume Card.

Can I add an existing Suica to my Fitbit device?

You must set up a new Suica in the Google Health app. You can’t add existing plastic or mobile Suica cards.

Note that even if you use Suica in another app on your phone, you must add a new Suica in the Google Health app to use Suica on your Fitbit device. Suica on your Fitbit device will have a different Suica ID number than your other cards.

Can I add a second Suica to my Fitbit device?

You can only add 1 Suica to your Fitbit device.

Do I need to have my phone nearby to use Suica on my Fitbit device?

You don’t need to have your phone nearby to use Suica on your Fitbit device. After you set up Suica, you can make payments from your device and leave your phone at home. However, to add funds to Suica or check your transaction history, you need to use the Google Health app on your phone.

What should I do if my Fitbit device runs out of battery during a trip?

Make sure your Fitbit device is charged before beginning your trip. If you can’t tap out of the station gate because your Fitbit device’s battery is completely drained, confirm with a JR East station agent to pay your fare in cash or other method. The next time you enter a station with your charged Fitbit device, ask a JR East station agent and explain that you tapped into the ticket gate without tapping out.

What should I do if I lose my Fitbit device?

If you lose or can no longer access your Fitbit device, contact Google Health Customer Support.

I want to give my Fitbit device to someone else—what should I do?

Before giving your Fitbit device to another person, remove Suica in the Google Health app. For instructions, refer to Then, follow the instructions in How do I erase my Fitbit device?

Note that erasing your Fitbit device doesn’t remove Suica. If you forget to remove Suica before erasing your device or giving it to someone else, Suica is removed from your Fitbit device when the device is set up on a new account. If your card is applicable for a refund, you’ll receive an email with a link to the refund request form.

If you reset your device using the same Google account, Suica remains on your device and you don’t need to set it up again.

Can I transfer Suica to a new Fitbit device?

You can’t transfer Suica to a new Fitbit device. If you switch to a new Fitbit device, set up a new Suica.

  1. Remove your existing Suica in the Google Health app. For more information, refer to
  2. Set up your new Fitbit device. For more information, refer to How do I set up my Fitbit device?
  3. Set up a new Suica. For more information, refer to
What should I do if Suica is disabled?

If you receive an error in the Google Health app that Suica is disabled, you can’t use it. Follow the on-screen instructions to remove Suica from your Fitbit device.

Set up a new card to continue using Suica on your Fitbit device. For more information, refer to

Why can’t I add funds to Suica on my Fitbit device?

If you encounter an error message when you try to add funds to Suica:

  1. Make sure your phone has a strong internet connection and try again.
  2. Make sure your Google Wallet account has a valid payment method and funds. For more information on using Google Wallet, refer to support.google.com.
Why don’t ticket gates and cash registers recognize my Fitbit device?

If you suspend your card in the Google Health app, ticket gates and cash registers don’t recognize your Fitbit device. Resume your card to reactivate it. For more information, refer to

If you haven’t used Suica on your Fitbit device recently, it’s automatically deactivated. To reactivate it, add funds to Suica in the Google Health app, or take your Fitbit device to a JR East station agent, and explain you haven’t used Suica recently.

What should I do if I receive an error or duplicate charges when I use my Fitbit device to pay at a store or vending machine?

You might receive an error if you move your Fitbit device away from the reader before the payment finishes processing. If you receive an incomplete payment error or duplicate charges, take your receipt to the store where the error occurred. If the error occurred while using a vending machine or coin locker, use the contact information displayed on the machine.

How do I request a receipt for Suica top-up transactions?
  1. Open the Google Health app .
  2. At the top left, tap Connections and then your device.
  3. Tap GoogleWalletRequest Receipts.

After you confirm you want to receive the receipts, you’ll receive an email.

Can I purchase a green ticket or commuter pass with Suica on my Fitbit device?

You can’t purchase green tickets or commuter passes at this time.

How do I use my Fitbit device to access the Shinkansen e-ticket service or Touch de Go! Shinkansen?

Register Suica on your Fitbit device with the service you want to access:

  • Shinkansen e-ticket service
  • Touch de Go! Shinkansen

Touch the Shinkansen automatic ticket gate with your Fitbit device.

Can I earn JRE Points with Suica on my Fitbit device?

You can earn JRE Points with Suica on your Fitbit device. For instructions on how to register, refer to jrepoint.jp.

Is there an annual fee for using Suica on my Fitbit device?

There’s no annual fee for using Suica on your Fitbit device.

What’s the maximum balance of Suica on my Fitbit device?

When you set up Suica, you can add up to ¥5,000. After you use Suica on your Fitbit device for some time, the maximum balance increases to ¥20,000.

Related resources

  • Pay with Suica on your smartwatch (Japan only)
  • Use Google Wallet for transportation

What should I know about using my Fitbit device to make contactless payments?

Add your credit and debit cards to certain Fitbit devices to make contactless payments right from your device—even when you’re traveling internationally.

Google Wallet is now available on Fitbit devices that support contactless payments. Set up Google Wallet in the Google Health app (version 4.27 or higher) to continue making contactless payments using your Fitbit device.

To check if your card works on your Fitbit device, refer to Supported payment methods on Fitbit.

Tip: This list is specifically for Fitbit devices and differs from the list of banks and countries compatible with Google Wallet on your phone.

Which Fitbit devices support contactless payments?

Make contactless payments with Fitbit Charge 4, Fitbit Charge 5, Fitbit Charge 6, Fitbit Sense, Fitbit Sense 2, Fitbit Versa 2, Fitbit Versa 3, Fitbit Versa 4, and editions of Fitbit Charge 3 and Fitbit Versa that contain an NFC chip.

Where can I use contactless payments?

Use your Fitbit device to purchase items in any store that accepts contactless payments or to ride select transit systems. To determine if the store accepts contactless payments, check for the symbol below on the payment terminal:

Screenshot: Icon that’s used on contactless readers, which looks like someone tapping a card

You can also use your Fitbit device on transit readers that accept contactless credit or debit card payments, such as Sydney’s ferry and light rail networks. For more details, refer to How do I use my Fitbit device to pay for transit?

Why is the Google Health app asking me to set up Google Wallet?

Google Health is updating our contactless payments feature to Google Wallet. This update will increase the number of banks and cards that are available for contactless payments on your Fitbit device and let you pay quickly everywhere Google Wallet is accepted. Google Wallet is available on Charge series, Sense series, and Versa series devices that support contactless payments.

To switch to Google Wallet:

  1. Open the Google Health app .
  2. At the top left, tap Connections and then your device and then Google and then Wallet.
  3. Tap Update to Google Wallet, and sign in to your Google account.
  4. Follow the on-screen instructions to add a card to Google Wallet.

After setting up Google Wallet, the Wallet tile in the Google Health app will change to the Google Wallet tile. For questions about Google Wallet that aren’t related to your Fitbit device, refer to Google Wallet Help.

Why can’t I view the Google Wallet tile?

If you don’t encounter the option to set up Google Wallet in the Google Health app:

  1. Check if Google Wallet is available in your country: Where you can use Google Wallet.
  2. Make sure your Fitbit device is up-to-date. For instructions, refer to How do I update my Fitbit device?
  3. If you recently updated your Fitbit device, wait 24 hours, and then check the Wallet again.
  4. Make sure you setup contactless payments. For instructions, refer to
Do I need to install the Google Wallet app on my phone?

You don’t need to install Google Wallet on your phone in order to use Google Wallet on your Fitbit device.

Does my Fitbit device use Google Wallet?
  1. Open the Google Health app .
  2. At the top left, tap Connections and then your device and then Google and then Wallet.
  • Confirm you use Google Wallet for contactless payments.
How do I set up contactless payments?

To start, add at least one credit or debit card from a participating bank in the Google Health app:

  1. Open the Google Health app .
  2. At the top left, tap Connections and then your device.
  3. Tap Google Wallet.
  4. Follow the on-screen instructions to add a payment card. In some cases, your bank may require additional verification. If you’re setting up contactless payments for the first time, you may be prompted to set a 4-digit PIN code for your device. Tip: The passcode protection must be enabled for your phone.
  5. After you add a card, follow the on-screen instructions to turn on notifications for your phone (if you haven’t already done so) to complete the setup.

You can add additional cards and choose which card to set as the default payment option on your device from the Google Wallet tile.

How do I make a payment with my Fitbit device?

  1. Open the payments screen on your device:

    • Charge 5 and Charge 6–Swipe down from the clock face and tap Payments or Google Wallet.
    • Versa, and Versa 2—Swipe down from the top of your screen. After your notifications appear, swipe down again to open the control center. Tap the Wallet icon .
    • Sense and Versa 3—Open the Wallet app . For faster access to payments, add it as a button shortcut in the Settings app and then Shortcuts.
    • Sense 2 and Versa 4–Open the Google Wallet app or Wallet app . For faster access to payments, add it as a button shortcut in the Settings app and then Shortcuts.
    • All other devices—When you’re ready to pay, press and hold the left button on your device for 2 seconds. Swipe to the payments screen if it’s not shown.

  2. If prompted, enter your 4-digit device PIN code. Your default card appears on the screen.

  3. To pay with your default card, hold your wrist near the payment terminal. To pay with a different card:

    • Charge 3 and Charge 4—Tap the screen to find the card you want to use, and then hold your wrist near the payment terminal.
    • Charge 5 and Charge 6—Swipe to find the card you want to use, and hold your wrist near the payment terminal.
    • Sense 2, Versa, Versa 2, and Versa 4—Swipe up to find the card you want to use, and then hold your wrist near the payment terminal.
    • Sense and Versa 3—Swipe up to find the card you want to use, and tap it. Then hold your wrist near the payment terminal.

    Screenshot: A person tapping their watch on a contactless reader

When the payment succeeds, your device vibrates and you’ll receive a confirmation on the screen.

If the payment terminal doesn’t recognize your Fitbit device, make sure the device face is near the reader and that the cashier knows you’re using a contactless payment.

Tip: The payments screen might be hidden if you haven’t set up contactless payments. If the payments screen does not appear, add a card to your Fitbit device by following the instructions on How do I set up contactless payments?

Customers in Australia: If you have a credit or debit card from an Australian bank, hold your device near the payment terminal to pay. If your card is from a bank outside of Australia, or if you wish to pay with a card that isn’t your default card, complete steps 1-3 above.

If the purchase amount exceeds $100 AU, follow the instructions on the payment terminal. If prompted for a PIN code, enter the PIN code for your card (not your device).

What can I do if my bank or card isn’t supported?

In many countries, you can use a payment app. Download the app on your phone, and connect your existing bank account. Add your new digital account to your Fitbit device by following the instructions in How do I set up contactless payments?

Tip: We are supporting new cards regularly. For example, support for American Express cards in the US will be available in the coming weeks.

For more information, refer to:

  • Revolut
  • Curve
  • Wise
How do I use my Fitbit device to pay for transit?

Use your Fitbit device to tap on and off at transit readers that accept contactless credit or debit card payments. To pay with your device, follow the steps listed in How do I make a payment with my Fitbit device?

Tip: Pay with the same card on your Fitbit device when you tap the transit reader at the start and end of your trip. Make sure your device is charged before beginning your trip.

Can I use my Fitbit device to pay with OMNY in New York City?

Use any supported card on OMNY readers at certain NYC MTA stations and buses. For more information about OMNY, refer to MTA’s related article.

Can I use my Fitbit device to pay for transit in Singapore?

Use your Fitbit device on trains and buses in Singapore. For a list of supported cards, check the Singapore section in the list of supported banks.

To pay with a Visa card that you added to your Fitbit device before February 26, 2019, remove the card in the Google Health app, and then add the card as if you’re setting it up for the first time. If you continue to have issues, contact your bank for more information.

How do I change the default card on my Fitbit device?

When you’re ready to pay, your default card appears on your device’s screen. To change your default card:

Google Wallet
  1. Open the Google Health app .
  2. At the top left, tap Connections and then your device.
  3. Tap Google and then Wallet.
  4. Tap the card you want to set as the default option.
  5. Tap Details.
  6. Tap Make default for contactless on watch.
How do I change the order of the cards on my Fitbit device?

To change the order of the cards on your device:

Google Wallet
  1. Open the Google Health app .
  2. At the top left, tap Connections and then your device.
  3. Tap Google Wallet. Your cards are listed in the order they appear on your Fitbit device.
  4. Hold and drag a card to change the order of the cards. Release the card in the position you prefer.
Do I have to enter a PIN code to make a payment?

When you set up contactless payments, you’re prompted to set a personal 4-digit PIN code.

To authorize a payment, enter your PIN code the first time you make a contactless payment since last taking off your device, or if it’s been 24 hours since you made a payment.

For more information on this feature, refer to How do I use the device lock on my Fitbit device?

Do I need to have my phone nearby to pay with my Fitbit device?

You don’t need to have your phone nearby to pay with your Fitbit device. After you set up contactless payments, you can make payments from your device and leave your phone at home.

Where can I view a list of transactions made with my Fitbit device?

Many banks allow you to view your 3 most recent transactions made with your Fitbit device in the Google Health app.

To check your recent transactions:

  1. Open the Google Health app .
  2. At the top left, tap Connections and then your device.
  3. Tap Google Wallet.
  4. Tap the card you added to your device and then swipe up to see your 3 most recent transactions.

If this feature isn’t available for your card, or if you want to check the history of your transactions, review your bank or credit card statement.

Why was my transaction declined?

If your payment was declined, contact your bank for more information.

Are contactless payments on my Fitbit device secure?

Google Wallet protects your payment info with multiple layers of security, using one of the world’s most advanced security infrastructures to help keep your account safe. When you pay in stores, Google Wallet doesn’t share your actual card number, so your information stays secure. Using contactless payments on your Fitbit device also requires you to use a personal 4-digit PIN code for an added layer of protection.

How do I remove a card from my Fitbit device?

After you delete a card, the card is removed from the Google Health app and you can no longer use it to make payments with your device.

  1. Open the Google Health app .
  2. At the top left, tap Connections and then your device.
  3. Tap Google Wallet.
  4. Tap the card you want to delete.
  5. Tap DetailsRemove payment method.

To suspend a card:

  1. Open the Google Health app .
  2. At the top left, tap Connections and then your device.
  3. Tap Google Wallet.
  4. Tap the card you want to suspend.
  5. Tap Suspend Card.

To unsuspend your card, repeat the steps above and then tap Unsuspend Card.

What should I do if I lose my Fitbit device?

If you lose your device, you can remove the cards you added to the device using the Google Health app. For instructions, refer to How do I remove a card from my Fitbit device?

You can still make payments using the physical debit or credit cards, so contact your bank if the cards were lost or stolen.

Keep in mind that no one can use your device to make a payment without first entering your personal 4-digit PIN code.

How do I reset the PIN code for my Fitbit device?

Reset the PIN code for your device in the Google Health app. For instructions, refer to How do I use the device lock on my Fitbit device?

Can I use my Fitbit device to make payments internationally?

You can use your Fitbit device when traveling internationally at stores that accept contactless payments. Note that foreign transaction fees may apply to purchases made internationally depending on your bank’s policy.

Do I earn points or rewards for purchases made with my Fitbit device?

When you make purchases with your Fitbit device, you’ll continue to earn points or rewards that your credit or debit cards provide.

Can I use a gift card with contactless payments?

Currently, gift cards don’t work with contactless payments.

I want to give my watch to someone else. What should I do?

Factory reset your device to erase apps and personal data from the device. For instructions, refer to How do I erase my Fitbit device?

Tip: If you use Suica on your Fitbit device, erasing your Fitbit device doesn’t remove Suica. Before giving your Fitbit device to another person, remove Suica in the Google Health app.

I entered my PIN code incorrectly. How do I unlock my watch with my phone?

If you enter an incorrect PIN code 10 times, you’re prompted to unlock your Fitbit device in the Google Health app. For instructions, refer to How do I use the device lock on my Fitbit device?

Why can’t I set up Google Wallet?

Google Wallet for Google Health may not yet be available in your region. We are working on expanding the availability of Google Wallet for Google Health.

    • For devices purchased before July 11, 2023: Visit Fitbit Limited Warranty.

For issues you cannot fix or for lost or damaged devices, review your Fitbit device warranty using the Google Hardware Warranty Center.

Check your Fitbit warranty

How do I recycle my Fitbit device?

  1. Before you recycle your Fitbit device, we recommend that you erase or factory reset it to protect your personal information. For instructions, refer to How do I erase my Fitbit device?
  2. Request a free shipping label from our third-party recycling partner (in association with Google). The prepaid shipping label is emailed to you. For instructions, refer to Learn about Google’s recycling program.
  3. Place your device in a box, attach the label, and following the shipping instructions, or drop it off at a collection site near you.

For more information about our commitment to sustainability, refer to Google’s Product Sustainability Approach.

Our Continued Commitment To Data Privacy and Security

We’re excited about the next step in achieving our vision of making the world healthier. In January 2021, Fitbit entered into a definitive agreement and was acquired by Google.

Read the full press release here.

What does the acquisition of Fitbit by Google mean for me and my Fitbit data?

You, our users, are at the center of everything we do, and it’s important that you know that your trust is central to our mission and has been since day one. This did not change by joining Google. We are committed to the same strong data privacy and security protections. You are in control of your personal data, and we remain transparent about the data we collect and why. We never sell your personal information, and health and wellness data will not be used for Google ads.

Please read our Fitbit Privacy Policy for more information on how we use and protect your personal information.

Does Google currently control my Fitbit data?

The Google Health app supports two types of accounts:

  • If you use a Fitbit account and haven’t moved your account to Google, then Google does not control your data.
  • If you use a Google Account to sign in to the Google Health app (either because you created your account after June 2023 or moved an existing Fitbit account), then Google is your data controller.

You can move Fitbit to your Google Account until July 15. To learn more about moving your account to Google, see How to move your Fitbit Account to a Google Account. Support of Fitbit accounts ended May 19, 2026. A Google Account will be required to use Google Health.

How is my personal data handled now that Fitbit has joined Google?

We are committed to strong data privacy and security protections. This did not change by joining Google. You are in control of your personal data, and we are transparent about we process your data.

Will Google use my Google Health data for advertising?

Health and wellness data is not used for Google ads.

What should kids and teens know about Fitbit’s privacy policies?

This article is meant to help kids and teens understand Fitbit’s privacy policies. If you sign in to the Fitbit app with a Google Account, see What should I know about my privacy on Fitbit?

For kids under 13 or older depending on where you live

The Fitbit Privacy Policy for kids’ accounts explains what information Fitbit receives about you and what we do with it. Here are some key points from that policy.

What information does Fitbit receive about me?

For you to use a Fitbit Ace tracker, first your guardian signs you up in the Fitbit app. During signup, your guardian provides us with some information about you, like what your first name is, when your birthday is, and how tall you are. We also receive information when you use Fitbit. Your tracker collects data to track your activity during the day, including your steps, sleep, active minutes, and more. Fitbit doesn’t receive location information for kids’ accounts.

What information does Fitbit share with my guardian about me?

Guardians control their children’s accounts within their family account. This means your guardian can see your complete account at any time through the family account. Your guardian can see how many steps you take, how many active minutes you get, and how much time you sleep each night.

What information can other people see about me?

Other members of your family account can see your username, your name, your picture, and your activity. If you add friends in the app, and your guardian approves them, they can see these things too.

Can I see my friends’ information in the Fitbit app?

You can add friends in the Fitbit app to see each other’s activity and information. Guardians have to approve the friend request before you can see each other’s information.

When does Fitbit stop sharing information about me with my guardian?

When you turn 13 (or older, depending on where you live), you can change your account to be a standard Fitbit account outside of your guardian’s family account. When you do this, your account will no longer be a child account, and your guardian will no longer be able to see your account information through their family account. If you still want your guardian to see information like how many steps you take each day, you can add them as a friend within your standard Fitbit account.

How do I ask Fitbit to delete my account information?

Your guardian can delete your account at any time through their family account or they can contact Customer Support

FOR TEENS 13 AND UP

The Fitbit Privacy Policy explains what information Fitbit receives about you, what we do with it, and what privacy controls you have. Here are some highlights from the policy and useful tips.

What information does Fitbit collect about me?

Daily stats

To use a Fitbit watch or tracker, you have to create an account in the Fitbit app. You’ll provide some information, including what your name is, when your birthday is, how tall you are, and how much you weigh. This information helps your Fitbit device to track your steps, sleep, and other activity. You can also choose to add profile and background pictures, a sentence or 2 about who you are, and where you live. The stats collected by your Fitbit device depend on which device you have. When your device syncs with the Fitbit app, the stats that your device collects are sent to our systems.

Location

Some Fitbit features use precise location information like GPS data, which lets you see a map of your route if you complete an exercise with GPS tracking turned on. You need a Fitbit device that supports GPS, or you can turn on this feature on your phone. If you don’t want to share your location, you can turn off location services for the Fitbit app on your phone.

Some other stuff

We collect data about how you use Fitbit, including which apps you install and which Fitbit Devices you use. We also receive information about the phone or computer you use with Fitbit, including your IP address and language, and the browser and operating system you use. To see a list of the Devices that are connected to your Fitbit account, go to this website.

We use the data that we collect in a few ways, including to provide you with Fitbit, improve our current features and products, and build new stuff that we hope you’ll like.

What information can other Fitbit users see about me?

After you sign up, there are some things that anyone who uses the Fitbit app can see about you, some things that only your friends can see, and some things that only you can see.

Here’s what everyone can see when you sign up:

  • Your first name and last initial (known as your Display Name)

  • Profile and background pictures, if you added them

  • The day you joined Fitbit

  • Your average daily step count

Here’s what only your friends can see when you sign up:

  • Fitness goals or other information you entered in the About Me section

Here’s what only you can see when you sign up:

  • Who your friends are on Fitbit

  • Where you live

  • Badges

  • Lifetime steps, distance, and floors

After signup, you can choose to make most of these things private or to share them with friends only. Here’s how to update your privacy settings in the Fitbit app:

  1. Tap the Today tab , and tap Devices .
  2. Tap Social & SharingPrivacy.
  3. Tap each item to review and adjust your privacy settings.

For more information, see How do I manage my Fitbit profile?

Are there any features that I can’t use?

There are a few features in the Fitbit app and on Fitbit Devices that aren’t available to teens, including the Fitbit ECG app and health coaching (where available).

How do I use the social features in the Fitbit app?

Community

You can post in the feed or in a group in the Fitbit community. Everyone who uses the Fitbit app can see your post in the feed, including your display name and profile picture. If you post in a group, everyone else in that group can see what you posted and your display name and profile picture.

Tell us if you see something that’s not quite right. We review reported posts, comments, and profiles as quickly as possible to check if someone broke our community guidelines.

You can report a post, comment, user, or group in the Fitbit app.

To report a post:

  1. Tap the 3 dots in the corner of the post you want to report.
  2. Tap Report Post.
  3. Select your reason for reporting the post, then tap Send Feedback.

To report a comment:

  1. Find the comment you want to report:
    • iPhones and iPads: swipe left on the comment, then tap Report.
    • Android phones: press and hold on the comment, then tap Report This Comment
  2. Select your reason for reporting the post, then tap Send Feedback.

To report a user in the Fitbit community:

  1. From their profile, tap the 3 dots.
  2. Tap Report Profile.
  3. Select your reason for reporting the user, then tap Send Feedback.

To report a group in the Fitbit community:

  1. From the group page, tap the 3 dots.
  2. Tap Report Group.
  3. Select your reason for reporting the group, then tap Send Feedback.

For more information, see What should I know about groups in the Fitbit Community?

Manage friends or block someone

Keep up with friends and family members by adding them as friends in the Fitbit app. You can also remove friends or block someone.

To add friends in the Fitbit app:

  1. Tap the Today tab , and tap Devices .
  2. Tap your nameAdd Friends.
  3. Choose a method to find friends, then tap the Add Friend icon next to the name or email address of the person you want to add.

To remove friends or block someone in the Fitbit app:

  1. Tap the Today tab , and tap Devices .
  2. Tap your name and scroll to see your friends.
  3. Tap View All Friends, then tap the friend you want to delete or block.
  4. On their profile, tap More.
    • To remove the friend, tap Remove Friend.
    • To block a friend, tap Block User.

To unblock someone in the Fitbit app:

  1. Tap the Today tab , and tap Devices .
  2. Tap Social & SharingBlocked Users
  3. Find the person you want to unblock Unblock and confirm.
  4. Confirm you want to send a friend request.

For more information, see How do I connect with friends on Fitbit?

Direct messages

You can send and receive direct messages from Fitbit friends. To send a message to someone, first you need to add them as a friend.

If you don’t want someone to send a message to you, remove them as a friend, or block them. Follow the steps above to block someone.

How do I turn my notifications on or off?

Notifications on your Fitbit device

You can see notifications about calls, text messages, and calendar events from your phone right on your wrist. These notifications are turned on automatically after setup. Choose to turn on notifications from apps like Messenger or WhatsApp so that you can see them on your Fitbit device instead of having to take out your phone.

You can answer or reject calls from your phone on your device’s screen. If you have an Android phone, you can also respond to messages from some apps with your device.

Set up and turn notifications on your device on or off in the Fitbit app:

  1. With your Fitbit device nearby, tap the Today tab , then tap Devices .
  2. Tap your device image Notifications. Follow the on-screen instructions to pair your Fitbit device to your phone.
  3. Choose the types of notifications you want to receive. Tap App Notifications and choose the apps you want notifications from.
  4. Sync your device.

For more information, see How do I get notifications from my phone on my Fitbit device?

Push and email notifications

We send notifications to your phone about your Fitbit activity, like updates about your weekly stats, new badges you get, and when your device’s battery is low. We also send emails about these things and about products you might like (more on that below) to the email address you used to sign up.

Turn push and email notifications on or off in the Fitbit app:

  1. Tap the Today tab and tap Devices .
  2. Tap Notifications.
  3. For each item, review and adjust your notifications settings.
How do I use contactless payments?

You can add a credit or debit card to some Fitbit Devices and use it to pay for purchases in a store. You can see the last 4 digits of your card number and a picture of your card type on your Fitbit device, but we don’t keep track of your full card number or what you buy. To use contactless payments, you need to set a PIN code, which is a 4-digit number that locks and unlocks your device. You can delete the card from your device in the Fitbit app.

If you want to use your guardian’s credit or debit card with contactless payments, first ask them if it’s okay. When you add their card to your device, your guardian has to approve it with their credit card company or bank.

For more information, see What should I know about using my Fitbit device to make contactless payments?

Does Fitbit share my data with anyone else?

We never sell your personal information. We don’t share your personal information except in the limited situations described in the Fitbit Privacy Policy.

If you choose to connect your Fitbit account with another app like MyFitnessPal or Peloton, you may authorize us to share your exercise or activity data with the other app, and the other app may share similar information with us.

You can stop an app from sharing data with Fitbit, or stop Fitbit from sharing data with another app, at any time.

For more information, see How do I connect Fitbit with another app?

We share data with trusted business partners that help us provide our product and services. For example, we share data on a confidential basis with our third-party customer support and billing service providers. We may also share data as required by law, for example, in response to a court order.

Does Fitbit use my data for marketing?

We may send marketing emails about stuff like new Fitbit watches or trackers to the email address you used to sign up. You can control these emails in the Fitbit app using the steps above, or scroll to the bottom of an email and tap Unsubscribe.

We may also use cookies, which are small pieces of data stored on your web browser or device, to show you ads for Fitbit products that we think you might like. You can control this use of cookies as described in the Your Choices section of the Fitbit Cookie Policy.

Can I download my Fitbit account data?

You can download your GPS data, community data, or an archive of your account data. To learn how, see How do I export my Fitbit data?

How do I delete my Fitbit account?

Delete your account in the Fitbit app:

  1. Tap the Today tab , tap your profile icon and Settings .
  2. Scroll down and tap Manage Data.
  3. Tap Delete account and follow the on-screen instructions.

Keep in mind that it can take a little while for us to delete all of your account details.

  • First 7 days: If you change your mind after you confirm your request to have your account deleted, you have 7 days to recover it—log in to your account to restore access to your Fitbit data.
  • After 7 days: Your account is frozen and can’t be recovered.
  • Within 30-90 days: Most of your personal account info is deleted within 30 days of when you confirm your deletion request. This includes any subscriptions you have. It may take up to 90 days to delete all of your personal info, like the data recorded by your Fitbit device and other data stored in our backup systems. This is due to the size and complexity of the systems we use to store data.
Where’s Fitbit located and how do I contact you?

For our location, see the Fitbit Privacy Policy for Children’s Accounts.

If you have any questions about our privacy policies, contact our Data Protection Officer at data-protection-office@fitbit.com.

Safety recalls

Safety Recall of Ionic Smartwatches

CONSUMER NOTICE

We announced a voluntary recall of Fitbit Ionic smartwatches, which the company introduced in 2017 and stopped producing in 2020. The battery in the Ionic smartwatch can overheat, posing a burn hazard.

The health and safety of Fitbit users is our highest priority. We are taking this action out of an abundance of caution for our users. We will offer a refund to Fitbit Ionic end-user consumers.

This recall is specific to Fitbit Ionic devices. It does not impact any other Fitbit smartwatches or trackers.

If you own a Fitbit Ionic, please stop using your device.

For information on how to receive a refund, visit our refund center.

Additional details regarding this recall are provided in the FAQ below. If you have any questions not answered below, you can call customer service. Click to find your local phone number.

USER FAQS

How do I get a refund?

To apply for your refund, visit our refund registration page to begin the refund process. After you complete the registration process, your registration will be reviewed if you are eligible for the refund.

If you are eligible for a refund, it’ll be issued by Google’s third-party vendor.

If you have questions about your Ionic, contact us. If you have questions about the status of your refund, contact us.

Important: Customer support may require you to provide proof of purchase or ownership.

Why did you do a recall?

After a thorough investigation, we determined that in very limited instances, the battery in the Ionic smartwatch can overheat, posing a burn hazard. Your safety is always our top priority, and we are taking this action out of an abundance of caution. We’re offering a refund to Fitbit Ionic end-user consumers.

My Ionic is working normally. Do I need to stop using it?

You should stop using your Ionic. We stopped producing Ionic in 2020 and aren’t offering replacement Ionic devices as part of this recall. For further information on how to receive a refund, visit our refund registration page.

If you have questions about your Ionic, contact us. If you have questions about the status of your refund, contact us.

Important: Customer support may require you to provide proof of purchase or ownership.

I don’t have an Ionic, but am wearing a different Fitbit device. Is my Fitbit device safe to wear?

This recall does not affect any other Fitbit smartwatches or trackers.

How do I know if I have Fitbit Ionic?

Check the image below to help you identify Ionic. Ionic has 3 buttons and a colored LCD.

You can find the model number FB503 on the back of Ionic, under the “CE” mark and above the clasp.

To check which device is connected to your Fitbit account:

  1. Tap the Today tab and then your profile picture.
  2. On the “Account” page, review the devices connected to your account.
What causes the problem with Fitbit Ionic?

After a thorough investigation, we determined that in very limited instances, the battery in the Ionic smartwatch can overheat, posing a burn hazard.

This recall does not affect any other Fitbit smartwatches or trackers.

Can I get a new Fitbit device?

We’re offering a refund to Fitbit Ionic end-user consumers. For further information on how to receive a refund, visit our refund registration page.

The best way to purchase a replacement device is to use the refund at the Google Store or your local Fitbit retailer. You can explore a range of Fitbit trackers and smartwatches and choose from the various options available.

Can I purchase a new Ionic?

You should stop using your Ionic. We stopped producing Ionic in 2020 and aren’t offering replacement Ionic devices as part of this recall. For further information on how to receive a refund, visit our refund registration page.

What are my options for compensation for Fitbit Ionic?

We’re offering a refund to Fitbit Ionic end-user consumers. For further information on how to receive a refund, visit our refund registration page.

What is my refund for Fitbit Ionic?

We’re offering a refund of 299 USD to Fitbit Ionic end-user consumers. For further information on how to receive a refund, visit our refund registration page.

I don’t know the email address for my Fitbit account associated with Ionic

For help with your account, contact us.

I have an Ionic I no longer use, can I get the refund?

Ionic users, including inactive users, who have purchased their device prior to the recall announcement and are in possession of the device, may be eligible for a refund. For further information on how to receive a refund, visit our refund registration page.

What’s the best device to purchase to replace Ionic?

Visit the Google Store or your local Fitbit retailer, where you can find details of the range of Fitbit trackers and smartwatches in order to make your own choice from the various options available. You can also take our quiz to find the best product for you!

How do I erase my personal information from my watch?

Erase the device to remove apps, stored data, personal information, credit and debit cards. For instructions, visit How do I erase my Fitbit device?

What happens to my Fitbit data if I consent to disabling syncing for my device?

Your Fitbit data remains associated with your Fitbit account. After we disable device syncing, new data from your device will no longer sync to your account. If you want to delete your Fitbit account, visit How do I delete my Fitbit account?

Where’s my refund?

If you have questions about your Ionic, contact us. If you have questions about the status of your refund, contact us.

Important: Customer Support may require you to provide proof of purchase or ownership.

What’s the difference between skin irritation and this issue?

Despite all our efforts, a small number of people may experience a reaction to certain materials. This reaction is typically due to eczema, allergies, or other skin sensitivities, which can become worse when irritants like sweat or soap get trapped beneath the band and irritate the skin. This recall is not related to skin irritation. If you have a Fitbit device and are experiencing skin irritation, review our Wear & Care instructions. Should your skin irritation not resolve, contact us.

Check the image below to help you identify Ionic. Ionic has 3 buttons and a colored LCD.

You can find the model number FB503 on the back of Ionic, under the “CE” mark and above the clasp.

To check which device is connected to your Fitbit account:

  1. Tap the Today tab and then your profile picture.
  2. On the “Account” page, review the devices connected to your account.
What causes the problem with Fitbit Ionic?

After a thorough investigation, we determined that in very limited instances, the battery in the Ionic smartwatch can overheat, posing a burn hazard.

This recall does not affect any other Fitbit smartwatches or trackers.

Can I get a new Fitbit device?

We’re offering a refund to Fitbit Ionic end-user consumers. For further information on how to receive a refund, visit our refund registration page.

The best way to purchase a replacement device is to use the refund at the Google Store or your local Fitbit retailer. You can explore a range of Fitbit trackers and smartwatches and choose from the various options available.

Can I purchase a new Ionic?

You should stop using your Ionic. We stopped producing Ionic in 2020 and aren’t offering replacement Ionic devices as part of this recall. For further information on how to receive a refund, visit our refund registration page.

What are my options for compensation for Fitbit Ionic?

We’re offering a refund to Fitbit Ionic end-user consumers. For further information on how to receive a refund, visit our refund registration page.

What is my refund for Fitbit Ionic?

We’re offering a refund of 299 USD to Fitbit Ionic end-user consumers. For further information on how to receive a refund, visit our refund registration page.

I don’t know the email address for my Fitbit account associated with Ionic

For help with your account, contact us.

I have an Ionic I no longer use, can I get the refund?

Ionic users, including inactive users, who have purchased their device prior to the recall announcement and are in possession of the device, may be eligible for a refund. For further information on how to receive a refund, visit our refund registration page.

What’s the best device to purchase to replace Ionic?

Visit the Google Store or your local Fitbit retailer, where you can find details of the range of Fitbit trackers and smartwatches in order to make your own choice from the various options available. You can also take our quiz to find the best product for you!

How do I erase my personal information from my watch?

Erase the device to remove apps, stored data, personal information, credit and debit cards. For instructions, visit How do I erase my Fitbit device?

What happens to my Fitbit data if I consent to disabling syncing for my device?

Your Fitbit data remains associated with your Fitbit account. After we disable device syncing, new data from your device will no longer sync to your account. If you want to delete your Fitbit account, visit How do I delete my Fitbit account?

Where’s my refund?

If you have questions about your Ionic, contact us. If you have questions about the status of your refund, contact us.

Important: Customer Support may require you to provide proof of purchase or ownership.

What’s the difference between skin irritation and this issue?

Despite all our efforts, a small number of people may experience a reaction to certain materials. This reaction is typically due to eczema, allergies, or other skin sensitivities, which can become worse when irritants like sweat or soap get trapped beneath the band and irritate the skin. This recall is not related to skin irritation. If you have a Fitbit device and are experiencing skin irritation, review our Wear & Care instructions. Should your skin irritation not resolve, contact us.

Settings

Accessibility features available on your Google Health service

On a computer

Learn about accessibility options and how to contact the Google Disability Support team.

Accessibility in the Google Health app

You can turn on common accessibility features in your device’s settings.

Explore the accessibility features available on the Google Health app.

Vision

  • To interact with the app with touch and spoken feedback, turn on the TalkBack screen reader in your device settings. TalkBack describes your actions and tells you about alerts and notifications.
  • To enhance or adjust the visible display in the app, you can:
    • Magnify your entire screen or parts of your display, including text or button sizes, through the display size and text settings.
    • Change font size, style, and contrast in the display size and text settings.
    • Adjust the app display to enhance your vision with color correction or filters including gray scale and color inversion in the color and motion settings.
  • You can select portions of the app to be spoken aloud by turning on Select to Speak.

Hearing

  • Pair hearing aids with your Android device to hear more clearly.
  • Turn on live captions from your Android settings. This will let you read the audio or video spoken content.

Touch

  • Use your voice to open and navigate the app and to edit text with Voice Access.
  • Interact with the app through an external switch or keyboard, or with the physical buttons on your phone when you turn on Switch Access in Android settings.

Voice

  • Use the app without voice commands.
Available accessibility service features on Health apps on Google Pixel Watch

Enhance your smartwatch health experience with these available accessibility options.
