Apps
MyFitnessPal

You can connect your third-party device and app to the Google Health app using Health Connect (Android phone) or Apple Health (iPhone). Once connected, your data will sync to the Google Health app through that connection.

Be sure to check that you have the right permissions enabled for the data you want to share.

Alternatively, you can also connect to the Google Health app through the MyFitnessPal app.

  1. Open the MyFitnessPal app.
  2. On Android devices, at the bottom of the home screen tap More . For iPhone or iPad, at the top right of your home screen, tap the Profile icon.
  3. Scroll down and tap Apps & Devices and then Google Health and then Connect.
  4. Complete the setup by following the on-screen instructions.

For additional details, please refer to: Fitbit FAQ and Troubleshooting – MyFitnessPal Help

Key metrics include:

  • Nutrition and hydration data
  • Calories burned
  • Exercise sessions logged in MyFitnessPal or collected by MyFitnessPal from other apps or devices
Key metrics shared from Google Health that can be made available in the MyFitnessPal app:
  • Steps
  • Calories burned
  • Exercise sessions
  • Sleep records
  • Blood glucose

Some third-party apps, including MyFitnessPal, may report the same meal through multiple connections. For example, a connected app may log what you’ve eaten directly to the Google Health app, then log it again via Health Connect. Google Health tries to remove duplicate data synced from multiple connections.

Strava

Important: Activities logged in Strava will no longer sync to Google Health via the Strava integration. We are working with Strava to enable more import options for activities logged in Strava.

The Strava and Google Health integration has been updated so that you can now automatically sync any activity you log in Google Health to Strava.

How does the updated integration compare to the previous one?
  • More activity types: The updated integration allows you to sync any activity type logged, with and without GPS, in Google Health to Strava. The previous integration supported bikes, runs, hikes, and walks with GPS only.
  • More control: You can now choose which activity types you want to sync to Strava.

To take advantage of the updates, below to update your connection. If you do not update your connection, only bikes, runs, hikes, and walks with GPS will continue to sync.

To connect and sync Google Health with Strava:

From the Google Health app:

  1. Open the Google Health app . At the top left, tap Connections
  2. Tap Partner apps or Apps and services.
  3. Tap Strava and follow the prompts to update your connection.
    • If not previously connected, you may find Strava under “Add connections.”
  4. When prompted, authorize Strava to link to your Google Account and follow the on-screen instructions. Then, tap Agree and continue.
  5. You may be redirected to Strava’s login page. Log in to your Strava account.
  6. To sync Google Health and Strava, review the on-screen permissions. Then, tap Authorize.
  7. A confirmation page will appear. Tap Done.
  8. Once connected, the Strava card will appear under “Connected.”

Once connected, new activities will sync automatically from Google Health to Strava. If you wish to export a previous activity from Google Health and upload it directly to Strava, please refer to Google Health’s instructions on data export.

From the Strava app:

  1. Open the Strava app.
  2. In the You tab, tap Settings and then Connect to an app or device and then Google Health.
  3. Follow instructions to authorize Google Health and Strava to connect.

Tip: The connection is forward moving, so only new activities will sync moving forward. Historical activities will not sync upon connecting.

Control what you share with Strava

Once connected, you can control what activity types Google Health syncs to Strava.

  1. Open the Google Health app . At the top left, tap Connections
  2. Tap Partner apps or Apps and services.
  3. Under “Connected,” tap Strava and then Activity writing.
  4. Choose to turn on and off activity types as required.
What can I do if my Google Health data is not syncing to Strava?
  • Try to reconnect your accounts and confirm you have accepted the option to Upload your activities from Google Health to Strava. Sync your Fitbit tracker or Pixel Watch with the Google Health app, and wait an hour.
  • Confirm that you are not recording the same exercise in the Strava app or any other fitness tracking app and the Google Health app simultaneously.
  • Confirm that you recorded a new exercise after connecting your accounts. Previous exercises won’t be uploaded.

If you do not have success with the steps above, you can use the TCX export from Google Health’s app and upload it to your Strava account using the steps below.

  1. Open the Google Health app and tap the Fitness tab .
  2. Select the activity that you want to export.
  3. Tap More and then Export.
  4. Share or save the file to your mobile device.
Strava and Health Connect and Apple Health

If you are an Android phone user, the Google Health app can import activities you log in Strava if you connect both Google Health and Strava to Health Connect.

If you are an iPhone user, the Google Health app can import activities you log in Strava if you connect both Google Health and Strava to Apple Health.

Strava does not import Google Health (Fitbit or Pixel Watch) activities from Health Connect or Apple Health. .

Note: If you are exporting exercises from Google Health to Strava and importing exercises from Strava to Google Health via Health Connect or Apple Health, you may see duplicate activity records in Google Health.

Disconnect apps and devices from your Google Health account

Disconnect Health Connect, Apple Health, and third-party apps
To disconnect Health Connect:
  1. Open the Google Health app .
  2. At the top left, tap Connections and then Partner apps.
  3. Tap Manage Health Connect.
  4. Scroll and tap Disconnect.
  5. Follow the on-screen instructions.

Upon disconnection, Health Connect card will be re-listed under “Add connections” in Connections and then Partner apps.

To disconnect Apple Health:
  1. Open the Google Health app
  2. At the top left, tap Connections and then Apps & services.
  3. Tap Apple Health to access Apple Health’s settings.
  4. Scroll, then tap Disconnect.
    • A warning that states “Disconnect from Apple Health?” will appear.
  5. Review the warning before you tap Disconnect.
    • Previously granted permissions will remain active in Apple Health unless you turn it off. New data will not sync, but permissions are still granted. To remove permissions, tap Open app. You’ll be redirected to the Apple Health app.

Upon disconnection, the Apple Health card will be re-listed under “Add connections” in Connections and then Apps and services.

To disconnect a third-party app:
  1. At the top left, tap Connections .
  2. Tap Partner apps or Apps and services.
  3. Tap the app you want to disconnect.
    • If directed to another list, find the app you want to disconnect and tap it.
  4. Scroll and tap Disconnect.
  5. Follow the on-screen instructions.

You don’t need to disconnect from your third-party account once you disconnect from your Google Health account.

Tip: To manage Health Connect, go to How do I use Health Connect in the Google Health app?

Troubleshoot apps connected to Google Health

  1. Make sure your Fitbit device syncs with your account. For troubleshooting information, go to Why won’t my Fitbit device sync?
  2. Unlink the app from your account. For instructions, go to .
  3. Reconnect the app with your account. For instructions, go to .

If you have trouble syncing Google Health with another app, contact the developer of the app.

Google Health API compliance and data access

Data shared with third-party developers is governed by the developers’ privacy policies and terms of service. Google Health cannot remove information they store once you give them permission to access your Google Health data. You can revoke access for an app at any time by managing your connections on the Google Health app.

Apps created by third-party developers must follow the API Terms of Service. If you believe an app is not following these policies, please contact our support team at https://developers.google.com/health/support. When a third-party app requests permission to access or modify your Google Health data, it lists the specific types of data it would like permission for. These permissions map to specific Google Health API requests the app will be able to make on your behalf.

For information on developing your own third-party app, go to developers.google.com/health.

Extend your Fitbit device’s battery life

Battery life is the amount of time your Fitbit device runs after it’s charged to 100%. To maximize battery life, turn off or reduce your use of certain features.

Estimated battery life for your Fitbit device

Because battery life is affected by use and other settings, actual results may vary.

  • Device Name
    • Battery Life
  • Google Fitbit Air**
    • Up to 7 days
  • Fitbit Sense* Fitbit Sense 2* Fitbit Versa 2* Fitbit Versa 3* Fitbit Versa 4*
    • 6+ days
  • Fitbit Versa Fitbit Versa Lite Edition
    • 4+ days
  • Fitbit Ace 3
    • Up to 8 days
  • Fitbit Inspire 2 Fitbit Inspire 3*
    • Up to 10 days
  • Fitbit Ace and Fitbit Ace 2 Fitbit Alta Fitbit Blaze Fitbit Charge 2 Fitbit Flex 2 Fitbit Ionic* Fitbit Inspire Fitbit Inspire HR Fitbit Luxe
    • Up to 5 days
  • Fitbit Alta HR Fitbit Charge 3 Fitbit Charge 4* Fitbit Charge 5* Fitbit Charge 6*
    • Up to 7 days
  • Fitbit One
    • Up to 2 weeks
  • Fitbit Zip
    • Up to 6 months
  • Fitbit Flyer
    • 6-hour playtime

We recommend that you use the charging cable that came with your device. Note that after several hundred charge cycles, your device may need to be charged more often.

*Using features such as always-on display and GPS require more frequent charging.

  • If you turn on always-on display:
    • Charge 5, Charge 6, Inspire 3, Sense 2, Versa 2, and Versa 4 have a battery life of up to 3 days.
    • Luxe, Sense, and Versa 3 have a battery life of up to 2 days.
  • If you use built-in GPS continuously:
    • Charge 4, Charge 5, and Charge 6 have a battery life of up to 5 hours.
    • Ionic has a battery life of up to 10 hours.
    • Sense, Sense 2, Versa 3, and Versa 4 have a battery life of up to 12 hours.

**Maximum battery life is approximate and is based on testing conducted in 2025 on pre-production hardware and software, using default settings with a median Fitbit Air user battery usage profile across features. Battery life depends on features enabled, usage, environment and many other factors. Use of certain features will decrease battery life. Actual battery life may be lower.

Tips to extend your Fitbit device’s battery life
Software updates and maintenance
  • Keep in mind that it can take up to 2 hours to charge your device to 100%. Do not charge your device in extreme temperatures below 32° F (0° C) and above 113° F (45° C). For more information, refer to How do I charge my Fitbit device?
  • Keep your phone updated. When you receive a notification to update your device’s operating system, follow the on-screen instructions to install it. For more information, refer to Check & update your Android version or Update your iPhone or iPad.
  • If you’re not currently using it, certain Fitbit devices can be turned off for long-term storage. For more information, refer to How do I turn off my Fitbit device?
Feature management
  • Turn off the Button Lock setting on Inspire 2 and Inspire 3. For more information, refer to How do I navigate my Fitbit device?
  • Turn off notifications you do not need, such as alerts from apps on your phone, alarms, and reminders to move. For more information, refer to:
    • How do I get notifications from my phone on my Fitbit device?
    • How do I manage alarms on my Fitbit device?
    • What are the reminders I see on my Fitbit device?
  • If you move your hands a lot, your device’s screen may turn on more often than you realize. Prevent screen activation each time you turn your wrist. For more information, refer to How do I see the time on my Fitbit device?
  • Use phone GPS on Charge 4, Charge 5, and Charge 6 to allow the tracker to connect to your nearby phone’s GPS sensors. For more information, refer to How do I use GPS on my Fitbit device?
  • Reduce your use of music control, music apps, on-wrist calls, contactless payments, and connected or built-in GPS.​
  • Remove Suica or iPass from your Fitbit device.
  • Tracking SpO2 data may require more frequent charging. Remove SpO2 tracking from your Fitbit device to extend your battery life. For more information, refer to How do I track blood oxygen saturation (SpO2) with my Fitbit device?
Display settings
  • Dim the screen or turn on auto brightness (available on certain Fitbit devices). In the Settings app on your device, find the brightness setting, and tap to change it.
  • Turn off the always-on display setting (available on certain Fitbit devices). For more information, refer to How do I see the time on my Fitbit device?
  • On certain Fitbit devices, you can change your Screen Timeout setting to adjust the amount of time your screen stays on. For more information, refer to How do I navigate my Fitbit device?
  • Consider changing your clock face, as animated clock faces may require more frequent charging. For more information, refer to How do I change the clock face on my Fitbit device?

If you still have trouble, contact Customer Support.

Store your Fitbit device for long-term use
  • If you want to store your device for several weeks or months, charge it to 100%, then turn off the device to avoid additional battery use. Note that you can only turn off certain Fitbit devices. For more information, refer to How do I turn off my Fitbit device?
  • Do not leave your device plugged in on the charging cable during storage.
  • For trackers, charge the device to 100% at least once every 6 months.
  • For watches, charge the device to 100% at least once per year.
  • Store your device in a cool, moisture-free place.

Get started with the Google Health Coach

The Google Health Coach is a Google Health Premium feature, built with Gemini that helps you reach your health and wellness goals. This tool in the Google Health app supports you in building healthy habits for fitness, nutrition, sleep, and mindfulness.

Your Google Health Coach provides informational guidance, not medical advice. Consult a healthcare provider before making any health plan changes.

Important: Google Health Coach isn’t intended to diagnose, treat, cure, or prevent any medical condition and should not be relied on for any medical purpose, nor is it authorized to provide professional pharmaceutical recommendations or assessments. Do not use your coach for a serious disease or condition. Your coach is AI and can make mistakes. Some content may not be suitable for everyone.

How to use the personal health coach in the Google Health app

Before you begin

The Google Health Coach requires a Google Health Premium subscription available in the Google Health app .

Important: Google Health Coach and our Premium coaching features are currently available only to users who have a Fitbit or Pixel Watch device and are over the age of 18. These features are available in the following countries:

You can access Google Health Premium if you’re at least 18 and live in:

Australia, Austria, Belgium, Brazil, Canada, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Hungary, India, Indonesia, Ireland, Italy, Japan, Latvia, Lithuania, Malaysia, Mexico, Netherlands, New Zealand, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Singapore, Slovakia, Slovenia, South Korea, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, Taiwan, United Kingdom, and the United States.

You can view, remove access to, or delete data you’ve shared with Google Health Coach at any time. To learn more about data usage and privacy, go to Manage your Google Health Coach data & personalization.

Get started with Google Health Coach

The Google Health Coach starts with a conversation about your goals, your challenges, and where you are with your health journey.

  1. If you’ve provided consent to turn on the Google Health Coach in the app, you will be able to chat with the coach to set up your goals and get personalized plans.
  2. Tap Chat with Coach.
  3. Discuss your goals, where you are starting from, and any barriers or challenges you may have.
  4. This information will be used by the coach to provide you a personalized plan towards your goals and also to help coach you better.
    • The information you provide is stored in the conversation transcripts found under Ask Coach History.
  5. If you choose to not chat with the coach during setup, you can always chat with the coach later to tell it your goals and get personalized plans. To do so, tap Ask Coach and say something like “Help me set up a goal” or “Set up a new plan towards my goals”. Tip: You can change or modify your suggested workout plan by tapping Ask Coach . You can also tell your coach about the changes you want to make or ask for its help to make changes.
Start a conversation with your coach.

Tap Ask Coach at any time to start a conversation with your coach. You can:

  • Ask about your data
  • Share changes in your routine
  • Update your fitness plan
  • Ask a question
  • Log a meal, workout, or more with text, a photo, or a file
Log your activities and progress with your coach

You can log your health and fitness data, such as activity, weight, and nutrition, either by manually entering the information directly into the relevant areas of the app or by having a conversation with your coach.

To log data, choose an option:

  • On the Today tab, tap Log below the focus metrics.
  • On the Fitness tab, tap Log activity for workout and movement tracking.
  • On the Health tab, tap Add from the focus areas such as Sleep, Metabolic, Nutrition, Cycle, Fitness and Temperature.

To log data for metrics like Weight or Sleep, go to the specific metric screen and tap .

Share images and PDFs with your coach

Important: The coach can’t analyze diagnostic medical images or evaluate photos of physical symptoms to provide clinical assessments.

You can share images and PDFs in coaching conversations to save time. To get started, you can upload the following:

  • Meal and workout logs: Share photos to log your data quickly.
  • Medical records: Add records to your coaching conversations and get insights
  • Real-time support: Share a menu for healthy options, a training plan for your schedule, or equipment photos to ask about safety.
Log conversationally

You can create or update logs by telling the coach what you want to track.

Tap Ask Coach to start a new conversation with the coach.

To log data through conversation:

  1. Type or speak what you want to log. For example, “Log that I ate two scrambled eggs for breakfast.” Tip: You can also update an existing log. For example, “Update yesterday’s run from 5.3 miles to 4.7 miles.”
  2. Tap the submit arrow above the keyboard.

To log data with files:

  • To make logging faster, include images or PDFs. For example, “Log my breakfast” with an image of your breakfast.
    • From the coach conversation, you can tap Add to take a photo, select gallery images, or browse files.
    • Use images to help log your data. You can share photos to track activities, sleep, food, weight, body fat, glucose, or hydration.
  • The coach may ask follow-up questions to gather required information and track your weekly targets. If this happens, provide the answers in the conversation.
  • Once the coach has the information it needs, it will confirm the action and summarize the log entry. Tap the log entry to check the full log details. To delete a log, tap the trash can at the top right of your log details screen.

Your coach can handle a wide range of general wellness questions. To help you get started or keep the conversation going, it also provides suggestions. You can ask about:

  • Analysis of and insights into your personal health data
    • Fitness stats
      • “Tell me about my weekly steps.”
      • “Is my fitness improving?”
    • Health stats
      • “What’s my resting heart rate trend in the past year?”
    • Sleep patterns
      • “How has my sleep been in the last month?”
  • Coaching toward specific health or fitness goals
    • “What can I do to increase my Cardio Load when working out?”
    • “Replace today’s upper-body workout with a 4-mile run.”
  • Create custom workouts
    • Chat to coach, or Tap the Create Workout button to open a conversation with Ask Health. Simply describe the session you want, such as “Make me a 20-minute Pilates session,” and your coach will generate a structured routine you can immediately play or save.

Receive personalized insights from Google Health Coach

Google Health Coach gives you suggestions based on your progress and data. These include:

  • Workout routines: Recommended workout routines or physical activity guidance.
  • Mindfulness: Mindfulness exercises or stress-reduction techniques.
  • Meal plans: Personalized meal plans or dietary suggestions.

Start a conversation with your coach from anywhere in the app by tapping Ask Coach . Learn more about things you can ask the Google Health Coach.

Set & track health goals

The Google Health Coach can help you set realistic health goals. Recommendations adapt and evolve as your needs and habits change over time.

Check your progress

Get a summary of your key health metrics in the dashboards and reports. The Google Health Coach helps you understand your data so you can:

  • Identify trends: Discover patterns in your activity, sleep, and heart rate.
  • Find focus areas: Locate where you are doing well or need more work.
  • Track your journey: Get pictures of your progress toward your goals.
Receive messages from your coach

You will receive personalized messages that adapt to you throughout the day.

Examples of messages you may receive:

  • Start your day right with a morning message about how well you slept and how physically ready you are for the day ahead.
  • After a workout, you’ll get a breakdown of your performance and tips for how to improve.
  • In the evening you’ll receive a recap of your day, including info about how your body responded to your activities and progress towards your fitness plan (if you have one).

Chat with the coach to stay on track with a personalized plan

After you have created a plan with the Google Health Coach, you can find your plan for the week, which includes your weekly targets and an associated set of recommended workouts on the Fitness tab .

Follow your workouts and workout plan from your coach

Coach guidance: Before you start a workout, the coach provides a personalized explanation with the routine organized into custom segments like warm up, cool down, core, upper body, and more.

Interactive execution: As you complete a workout, check off your exercises one by one and log your reps and weights directly in the app.

View options: Workouts default to a full-screen interactive view. You can minimize this player to get the full workout as a list and check off individual exercises as you go.

Workout feedback: As you finish, rate your workout to indicate session difficulty. This feedback helps your coach provide more personalized recommendations in the future.

Save workouts: You can save your favorite workouts from the coach by selecting the bookmark icon at the top of the workout overview. You can then access these workouts in “Saved workouts”.

Merge a completed workout started on a device & mobile

If you tracked a workout on your watch without starting the guided phone experience, you can still merge those recorded metrics with your coach’s planned session afterward. This allows you to see your actual performance data and the intended workout structure in a single, unified view.

  1. In the Fitness tab, tap the recommended workout you completed.
  2. On the workout overview page, tap I have done this workout.
  3. Select the recorded session from your activity history to link it.
Adjust your plan & workouts conversationally or manually (Premium only)

You can adjust your plan, targets, and workouts at any time by talking to the coach directly or selecting the “Adjust” buttons.

  1. Make changes

    For a flexible experience, you can talk to the coach directly to request changes in your own words. You can also tap Make changes on the Fitness tab. Talking to the coach is best for adjusting to real-life situations, such as:

    • “I’m traveling this week, can we adjust my plan accordingly?”
    • “The treadmill is busy today”
    • “I’ve injured my foot”
    • “Make this workout longer” or “make it easier”

  2. Adjust a specific workout

To change one workout recommended by the coach, talk to your coach about the change. You can also tap Adjust on the workout overview screen.

You can also manually edit your workouts:

  • Movement details: Change the reps, sets, weights, or duration.
  • Exercise list: Add, reorder, or delete individual exercises. Important: Do not rely on the coach to determine the safety of an exercise if you’re in pain. Seek professional advice as needed.
Troubleshoot a missing workout plan

If you successfully set up the personal health coach but don’t see your weekly workout plan:

  1. In the Google Health app , tap your profile picture.
  2. Tap Google Health settings and then Activity.
  3. Scroll to the bottom and tap Regenerate weekly plan.
  4. Wait up to 10 minutes for your workout plan to show up on the fitness tab.
For Public Previews users looking for their previously available scheduled weekly workouts

For Public Preview users only: Previous scheduled plans are being retired. You can still download or delete your completed plans.

  • To export your data:
    1. In the Google Health app , tap your profile picture and then Google Health settings .
    2. Tap Manage data and privacy and then Export your data and then Export your data.
    3. Follow the instructions to export your selected data.
Leave your fitness plan

If you want to stop your current fitness plan and stop receiving tailored workout recommendations, you can leave the plan at any time:

  1. In the Google Health app , tap the Fitness tab .
  2. Tap on your active plan to open the plan details screen.
  3. Scroll to the bottom of the screen.
  4. Tap Leave plan to terminate your active coaching plan.

How do Fitbit devices sync their data?

Sync your device with the Google Health app on your iPhone or Android phone.

What is syncing?

Syncing is the process that transfers the data your device collects to your Google Health account. Track your progress, see how you slept, set goals, log food and water, and more in the Google Health app.

Fitbit trackers, watches, and Fitbit Aria Air use Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) technology to sync with phones and tablets. Fitbit Aria and Fitbit Aria 2 use Wi-Fi to connect directly to your router.

Visit the store to view our catalog of compatible devices.

How do I sync my device with the Google Health app?
Fitbit devices

Data automatically syncs to the Google Health app throughout the day. Each time you open the Google Health app, your device syncs automatically when it’s nearby.

For more information on how to sync Fitbit Ace devices, see How do I set up Fitbit Ace devices?

Google Pixel Watch series

Data automatically syncs to the Google Health app on your phone throughout the day and after you complete an exercise.

How do I manually sync my tracker or watch?
Fitbit devices and Google Pixel Watch
  1. With your device nearby, open the Google Health app on your phone.
  2. On the Today tab , tap and hold on the screen and pull down.

Or use the Sync Now option:

  1. Open the Google Health app .
  2. At the top left, tap Connections and then Sync .
When does my Fitbit scale sync?

Fitbit Aria or Fitbit Aria 2 automatically syncs your stats to the Google Health app after every weigh-in.

Screenshot: Illustration of the scale’s screen with a progress bar at the top and, below that, circular arrows in a counter-clockwise direction

A checkmark appears after data is synced. See your stats in the Google Health app.

Where can I see when my Fitbit device last synced?

Find information about your Fitbit device, such as firmware version, battery level, and when your device last synced.

Google Health app
  1. Open the Google Health app .
  2. At the top left, tap Connections and then your device.
  3. You will find the “last synced when” notification below your device’s image.
Why can’t I sync my Fitbit device?

If your device stopped syncing, the likely problem is a connection issue. For troubleshooting tips, see Why won’t my Fitbit device sync?

Can I sync my tracker or watch with more than one device?

Sync your device with any compatible phone or tablet. If you receive notifications on your Fitbit device, forget the Fitbit device under the Bluetooth settings on your phone before you use a different phone. For instructions see Why won’t my Fitbit device sync?

Can I sync more than one Fitbit device to the same account?

Multiple Fitbit devices can sync to the same account for a complete view of your activity. For more information, see How do I set up my Fitbit device?

How do I clean my Fitbit device?

Be sure to follow our Wear and Care instructions to keep your device clean.

Choose your device for more information.

Trackers and watches

We recommend that you occasionally:

  • Clean the charging contacts on the back of your device to ensure they stay bronze or gold in color:
    1. Use a toothbrush with freshwater. Dry with a cloth or tissue before charging.
    2. Make sure not to scrape the contacts with anything metal, since metal can damage the plating and cause corrosion.
  • Clean the pins on your charging cable:
    1. Clean the pins carefully with a cotton swab and rubbing alcohol.
    2. Make sure that no pieces of the swab are left behind.

Fitbit devices that count floors have a small hole (altimeter sensor) on the back of the device. Don’t insert any items, such as paper clips, into this hole as you can damage your device.

For additional cleaning instructions, see our Wear and Care page.

Scales

Clean your scale as needed to remove dust and soil. To clean your scale:

  • Wipe down the surface with a damp cloth using a mild detergent before your first use.
  • Do not submerge your scale or use high-pressure water jets (like a shower head) to clean the surface.
  • Do not use antiseptic wipes, chlorine, or highly concentrated glass cleaner on the surface of the scale.
  • Do not use abrasive cleaners to clean your scale.
Headphones

We recommend that you occasionally:

  • Remove the ear tips and wings or fins from Fitbit Flyer and wash them with water or a wet cloth. Allow them to dry completely before reattaching them to the headphones.
  • Clean the headphones with a soft, damp cloth. Use water only. The headphones are designed to be rain, sweat, and splash-proof, but shouldn’t be submerged in water.

How do I set up Fitbit Ace devices?

Learn how to set up and sync Ace, Ace 2, or Ace 3 for your child. If your child doesn’t have a Fitbit device, use the Google Health app on their phone to track their steps.

For assistance with Fitbit Ace LTE, go to support.google.com/fitbitacelte.

I’m setting up a kids tracker for the first time

Parents or guardians need:

  • Your child’s Ace tracker

  • Google Account with:

    • Google Health profile in the Google Health app

    • Google family group where you’re the family manager

  • Phone or tablet to set up your child’s Google Health profile and Ace tracker:

    • iPhone or iPad

    • Android phone or tablet

My child has their own phone or tablet
  1. Confirm that you are the family manager of a Google family group. For instructions on how to create a family on Google, see the Google for Families help center.
  2. Connect your child’s Ace device to the charger before you begin the setup process.
  3. Download and install the Google Health app from one of the following locations:
    • Apple devices—Apple App Store
    • Android devices—Google Play Store
  4. Tap Sign in with Google. Your child signs in with their Google Account. If your child doesn’t have a Google Account, tap Create your account, and follow the on-screen instructions.
  5. Review the information about managing a child account on Google Health.
  6. Tap Agree and continue, and enter the password for your Google Account.
  7. Add a Google Health profile for your child.
  8. Tap Next. Your child can log in to their Google Health profile.
  9. Tap Continue, and follow the on-screen instructions to pair Ace to your child’s profile.

Note: Ace syncs every time your child opens the Google Health app.

For more information on Google Accounts for children, see the Google for Families help article.

I’ll use my phone or tablet
iPhone or iPad
  1. Confirm that you are the family manager of a Google family group. For instructions on how to create a family on Google, see the Google for Families help center.
  2. Connect your child’s Ace device to the charger before you begin the setup process.
  3. Make sure you have a Google Health profile. If not, download the Google Health app and then tap Sign in with Google and then follow the on-screen instructions to create a profile. Please note that you do not need to have a Fitbit device in order to create a free account.
  4. In the Google Health app, tap your Profile picture or Initial.
  5. Tap Google Health settings and then Add a child account.
  6. Review the information about managing a child account on Google Health.
  7. Tap Agree and continue, and enter the password for your Google Account.
  8. Tap Continue, and follow the on-screen instructions to pair Ace.

Note: Ace syncs every time your child opens the Google Health app.

Android phone or tablet
  1. Confirm that you are the family manager of a Google family group. For instructions on how to create a family on Google, see the Google for Families help center.
  2. Connect your child’s Ace device to the charger before you begin the setup process.
  3. Make sure you have a Google Health profile. If not, download the Google Health app and then tap Sign in with Google and then follow the on-screen instructions to create a profile.
  4. Open the Google Health app and tap your Profile picture or Initial.
  5. Tap Google Health settings and then Add a child account.
  6. When prompted, enter your Google Health password and your child’s information.
  7. Switch to your child’s profile to set up the Ace device.

To sync Ace, switch to your child’s profile on your phone or tablet and then open the Google Health app. Ace syncs automatically.

Why do I need to update the birthday for my child’s Google Account?

Some parents might have previously created a Google Account for their child with an adult’s date of birth due to past technical limitations. Going forward, children now need to use Google Health with a Google Account birthday that matches their real date of birth.

To change your child’s birthday:

  1. Sign in to your child’s Google account.
  2. In a browser window, visit the Google Account Manager.
  3. Click Personal Info and then Birthday.
  4. Update the birthday and then Save.
Why can’t I set up my Ace 3 in Quebec?

Fitbit began requiring new child accounts to be registered with Google in June 2023. At this time, child registration isn’t supported in Quebec.

If you aren’t able to set up Ace 3 in Quebec due to this change, you may be eligible for a refund. Return your device to the original retailer if your purchase was made within their return window. Otherwise, contact customer support at contact.fitbit.com.

Note: When you contact customer support, provide proof of purchase and your shipping address. If you’re eligible for a refund, you’ll be provided with a prepaid shipping label to return your device.

How do I set up my Fitbit device?

On a computer

Use your phone to set up your Fitbit device. To verify that your phone is compatible with the Google Health app, go to Google Health setup requirements.

Set up your watches and trackers

Fitbit watches and trackers
Add or replace a Pixel or Fitbit device on an existing account
  1. Open the Google Health app
  2. At the top left, tap Connections and then Add device.
  3. Choose your device and follow the on-screen instructions to continue.

Once connected, your device will be listed under “Devices.” Details such as your device’s last synced time and battery percentage will appear.

If you already have a device paired and want to replace or pair a different one, tap Add more devices.

If you encounter issues with your Fitbit device setup, refer to Why can’t I set up my Fitbit device?

Set up a Fitbit device on a new account

When you connect certain Fitbit devices to your phone, a notification will appear to begin the setup process. Tap the notification and follow the instructions to set up your device. If you don’t receive a notification:

  1. Before you begin the setup process, connect your Fitbit device to the charger.
  2. Download and install the Google Health app from the Google Play Store.
  3. Open the Google Health app and tap Sign in with Google.
  4. Choose a Google Account. If you don’t have a Google Account, tap Sign in and then Create account.
  5. Follow the on-screen instructions to create an account and connect your Fitbit device to your phone. This ensures your Fitbit device and phone communicate with one another and sync data.

To complete the creation of your Google Health account, you’re prompted to enter your height, weight, and sex to calculate metrics like your stride length and estimate distance, basal metabolic rate (BMR), and calorie burn. For details, go to How does my Fitbit device calculate my daily activity?

Fitbit Ace

These instructions are only for Ace, Ace 2, and Ace 3. For assistance with Fitbit Ace LTE, visit Fitbit Ace LTE Help Center.

If you already use the Family option in the Google Health app, refer to How do I set up Fitbit Ace devices?

For the best experience, your child should have their own phone or tablet to set up an Ace device. If you have an iPhone or iPad, you can use your phone or tablet to set up your child’s device.

  1. Connect your child’s Ace device to the charger before you begin the setup process.
  2. Download and install the Google Health app from one of these locations:
    • Apple devices: Apple App Store
    • Android devices: Google Play Store

    • If your child doesn’t have a Google Account:
      1. Tap Sign in and then Create your account and then For my child.
      2. Follow the on-screen instructions.
  4. When prompted, review the information about managing a child account.
  5. Tap Agree and continue and enter the password for your Google Account.
  6. Add a Fitbit profile for your child.
  7. Tap Next. Your child can log in to their Fitbit profile.
  8. Tap Add device, and follow the on-screen instructions to pair Ace to the account.

For more information on Google Accounts for children, go to the Google for Families help article.

Google Pixel Watch
  1. Before you begin the setup process, connect Google Pixel Watch to the charger.
  2. Press the crown of your Google Pixel Watch for 3 seconds to turn it on.
  3. Place your watch near a compatible Android phone with Bluetooth on. A notification appears on your phone to begin the setup process.
  4. Install the Google Pixel Watch app. Then, follow the on-screen instructions to connect your watch to your Google Account. For more information or troubleshooting tips, go to Set up Google Pixel Watch.
  5. After you set up your watch, connect your account.
I need to create an account
  1. Download the Google Health app on your phone.
  2. Open the Google Health app , then tap Sign in with Google.
  3. Choose a Google Account. If you don’t have a Google Account, tap Sign in and then Create account.

I have an account

At the top left, tap Connections .

Tip: If prompted, follow the instructions to move Fitbit to your Google Account.

  1. Tap Add device and then Google Pixel Watch.

Once connected, your Google Pixel Watch will be listed under “Devices.” Details such as your device’s last synced time and battery percentage will appear

If you have issues with your watch and account setup, make sure the Google Health app on your watch is updated. After you update, try to connect your watch again:

  1. Press the crown, swipe up to the Play Store app , then tap the app to open it.
  2. Swipe up and tap Manage apps and then Update all.

If you’re still unable to connect your watch:

  1. Press the crown, swipe up to the Google Health app , then tap the app to open it.
  2. Swipe to the bottom, then tap SignIn.
  3. If prompted, download and install the Google Health app on your phone.
    • If you already have an account, sign in. If prompted, follow the on-screen instructions to move Fitbit to your Google Account.
    • If you don’t have a Google Health account, tap Sign in with Google then follow the on-screen instructions.
  4. Tap Devices and then Add device or Add more devices.
  5. Tap Google Pixel Watch in the list of devices and follow the on-screen instructions to connect your watch to your account.

When you create an account for Fitbit, you’re prompted to enter your height, weight, and sex. This will allow Fitbit to calculate your stride length, estimate distance, BMR, and calorie burn. For more information, go to How does my Fitbit device calculate my daily activity?

Multiple Fitbit devices on one Google account

With the exception of using 1 Fitbit Air and 1 Pixel Watch together, you can only connect one Fitbit device or Pixel Watch to an account at the same time in the Google Health app. Learn how to use Google Fitbit Air with a Google Pixel Watch in the Google Health app.

Scales

Important: If you’re unsure which scale you own, turn the scale over and remove the battery cover to check how many batteries it contains:

  • Aria uses 4 AA batteries
  • Aria 2 uses 3 AA batteries and has “Aria 2” written on the back of the scale
  • Aria Air uses 3 AAA batteries

For more information about how to use your scale, go to How do I use my Fitbit scale?

Aria
What router settings do I need to set up and sync Aria?

Aria connects to your wireless home network and works with any Wi-Fi router that uses these standards:

  • 802.11b frequency setting
  • WEP / WPA / WPA2 personal security
  • Automatic (DHCP) IP setup (static IP configurations aren’t supported)

Your SSID and password should contain only alphanumeric characters (for example, A to Z and 0 to 9). If you experience issues with a network that uses special characters, change the name of the network to only use alphanumeric characters, and try to connect again.

Can I use a mobile Wi-Fi hotspot to set up Aria?

A mobile Wi-Fi hotspot should only be used if a wireless router is unavailable. Consider these information when you set up your scale through a hotspot:

  • Connecting Aria to a mobile Wi-Fi hotspot requires that the mobile device be persistently in this mode. The device’s battery may drain quickly.
  • To complete the setup process with a mobile Wi-Fi hotspot, you need a second wireless device to connect to the hotspot. For example, if you use an iPhone as a hotspot, you need either another mobile device or a computer to proceed through either of the set up methods explained in
  • Your hotspot needs to be configured similar to the same specifications as a wireless router. For the specs, go to
How do I set up Aria?

To set up your scale through the web-based method, you need a Wi-Fi enabled computer, phone, or tablet. Make sure you know your Wi-Fi password and that it doesn’t exceed 31 characters.

Tip: If you want to set up your Aria again after you make changes to your network, go to How do I use my Fitbit scale?

To set up your Aria scale:

  1. Restart the computer, phone, or tablet that you want to use to set up your scale.
  2. Make sure your browser allows cookies.
  3. If you use a computer:
    1. Place your scale within 10 feet of your router.
    2. Ensure that your router is compatible with the 802.11b protocol. For more information, go to
    3. If the router is connected to your computer with an Ethernet cable, unplug it. The router and computer must be connected over Wi-Fi.
  4. Open a web browser on your computer, phone, or tablet and go to Fitbit scale setup.
  5. Tap Get started, then tap it again when you find the pop-up message.
  6. Sign in to your fitbit.com account.
  7. Personalize your Aria with a name and the initials you’d like the scale to display when it recognizes you.
  8. Remove a battery from your Aria scale and reinsert it after 10 seconds to put the scale into setup mode. Tap Continue when the scale’s display says “SETUP ACTIVE.”
  9. Switch your computer, phone, or tablet to the scale’s Wi-Fi network (this will appear as the word “Aria” followed by 6 characters).
  10. Return to your web browser and tap I’m Connected. You’ll find a list of available wireless networks.
  11. Tap the name of your home wireless network. If you can’t find your home wireless network, tap Refresh Networks to scan again. If you still can’t find your network, tap Join Other Network to enter your network name and password manually.
  12. Enter your network password. Remember that it’s case-sensitive.
  13. Tap Submit and then immediately check your scale’s screen as it attempts to connect to your network.
    • If you find a check mark or a smiley face, Aria is connected and you can stand on the scale to complete a weigh-in.
    • If you find an error message, go to How do I use my Fitbit scale?
Aria 2

To set up your Fitbit Aria 2, create an account. If you don’t have one, connect your scale through the Google Health app on your phone.

Router settings

Aria 2 connects to your wireless home network and works with any Wi-Fi router that uses these standards:

  • 802.11b/g/n frequency setting
  • WEP / WPA / WPA2 personal security
  • Automatic (DHCP) IP setup (static IP configurations aren’t supported)
  • Both the network name and password must be no more than 32 characters long

We don’t recommend a mobile Wi-Fi hotspot to set up Aria 2, as it may slow down the sync process and prevent an update. The use of a mobile Wi-Fi hotspot requires the device to remain persistently in this mode, which may drain the battery quickly and use excessive data.

Set up Fitbit Aria 2 on a new account

Important: If you want to set up your Aria 2 again after you make changes to your network, go to How do I use my Fitbit scale?

  1. Make sure the Google Health app is compatible with your device. To check, go to Google Health setup requirements.
  2. Download and install the Google Health app from the App Storeor Play Store.
  3. Open the Google app and tap Sign in with Google.
  4. Choose a Google Account. If you don’t have a Google Account, tap Sign in and then Create account.
  5. Follow the on-screen instructions to create a Google Health account and connect your scale to the internet. You must know your wireless network password and the scale must be within range of the network. If you find an error message, go to How do I use my Fitbit scale?

Note that the personal information you provide to set up your account is used to calculate your BMR. This helps determine your estimated calorie expenditure and your body mass index (BMI). For more information, go to How does my Fitbit device calculate my daily activity?

If you have trouble setting up Aria 2, briefly press the button in the battery compartment to restart your scale and begin the process again. If you still can’t set up your Aria 2 upon completion of the steps above, contact Customer Support.

Add Aria 2 to an existing account

At the top left, tap Connections .

  1. Under “Devices,” tap Add device.
  2. Choose your device.
  3. Follow the on-screen instructions to create a Google Health account and connect your scale to the internet. You must know your wireless network password, and the scale must be within range of the network.

If you have trouble setting up Aria 2, briefly press the button in the battery compartment to restart your scale and begin the setup process again.

Personalized icon on Aria 2

When you set up your scale, you’re asked to choose a personalized icon. This icon appears on the scale whenever you complete a weigh-in. After you weigh yourself, you can check your icon on the screen to confirm if the weigh-in is assigned to the correct person. Refer to the table for a complete list of the available icons.

At the top left, tap Connections .

On the back of your scale, find the battery compartment and pull out the plastic tab. This should turn your scale on.

Remove a Fitbit device from an account

When you remove a Fitbit device from your account, any data you haven’t synced is deleted. For more information about syncing, go to How do Fitbit devices sync their data?

If you’ll give your Fitbit device to someone else, erase your data before removing the device from your account. For instructions, go to How do I erase my Fitbit device?

Google Health app

At the top left, tap Connections .

  1. Under “Devices,” you’ll find the list of devices linked to your app. Tap the device you want to remove.

    • For Pixel devices, tap Disconnect devices.

  3. Follow the on-screen instructions to remove the device from your account.
fitbit.com
  1. On the Fitbit settings page, click your device in the Devices section.
  2. At the bottom of the page, click the option to remove the device.
  3. Follow the on-screen instructions to remove the device from your account.

Once connected, your Google Pixel Watch will be listed under “Devices.” Details such as your device’s last synced time and battery percentage will appear

If you have issues with your watch and account setup, make sure the Google Health app on your watch is updated. After you update, try to connect your watch again:

  1. Press the crown, swipe up to the Play Store app , then tap the app to open it.
  2. Swipe up and tap Manage apps and then Update all.

If you’re still unable to connect your watch:

  1. Press the crown, swipe up to the Google Health app , then tap the app to open it.
  2. Swipe to the bottom, then tap SignIn.
  3. If prompted, download and install the Google Health app on your phone.
    • If you already have an account, sign in. If prompted, follow the on-screen instructions to move Fitbit to your Google Account.
    • If you don’t have a Google Health account, tap Sign in with Google then follow the on-screen instructions.
  4. Tap Devices and then Add device or Add more devices.
  5. Tap Google Pixel Watch in the list of devices and follow the on-screen instructions to connect your watch to your account.

When you create an account for Fitbit, you’re prompted to enter your height, weight, and sex. This will allow Fitbit to calculate your stride length, estimate distance, BMR, and calorie burn. For more information, go to How does my Fitbit device calculate my daily activity?

Multiple Fitbit devices on one Google account

With the exception of using 1 Fitbit Air and 1 Pixel Watch together, you can only connect one Fitbit device or Pixel Watch to an account at the same time in the Google Health app. Learn how to use Google Fitbit Air with a Google Pixel Watch in the Google Health app.

Scales

Important: If you’re unsure which scale you own, turn the scale over and remove the battery cover to check how many batteries it contains:

  • Aria uses 4 AA batteries
  • Aria 2 uses 3 AA batteries and has “Aria 2” written on the back of the scale
  • Aria Air uses 3 AAA batteries

For more information about how to use your scale, go to How do I use my Fitbit scale?

Aria
What router settings do I need to set up and sync Aria?

Aria connects to your wireless home network and works with any Wi-Fi router that uses these standards:

  • 802.11b frequency setting
  • WEP / WPA / WPA2 personal security
  • Automatic (DHCP) IP setup (static IP configurations aren’t supported)

Your SSID and password should contain only alphanumeric characters (for example, A to Z and 0 to 9). If you experience issues with a network that uses special characters, change the name of the network to only use alphanumeric characters, and try to connect again.

Can I use a mobile Wi-Fi hotspot to set up Aria?

A mobile Wi-Fi hotspot should only be used if a wireless router is unavailable. Consider these information when you set up your scale through a hotspot:

  • Connecting Aria to a mobile Wi-Fi hotspot requires that the mobile device be persistently in this mode. The device’s battery may drain quickly.
  • To complete the setup process with a mobile Wi-Fi hotspot, you need a second wireless device to connect to the hotspot. For example, if you use an iPhone as a hotspot, you need either another mobile device or a computer to proceed through either of the set up methods explained in
  • Your hotspot needs to be configured similar to the same specifications as a wireless router. For the specs, go to
How do I set up Aria?

To set up your scale through the web-based method, you need a Wi-Fi enabled computer, phone, or tablet. Make sure you know your Wi-Fi password and that it doesn’t exceed 31 characters.

Tip: If you want to set up your Aria again after you make changes to your network, go to How do I use my Fitbit scale?

To set up your Aria scale:

  1. Restart the computer, phone, or tablet that you want to use to set up your scale.
  2. Make sure your browser allows cookies.
  3. If you use a computer:
    1. Place your scale within 10 feet of your router.
    2. Ensure that your router is compatible with the 802.11b protocol. For more information, go to
    3. If the router is connected to your computer with an Ethernet cable, unplug it. The router and computer must be connected over Wi-Fi.
  4. Open a web browser on your computer, phone, or tablet and go to Fitbit scale setup.
  5. Tap Get started, then tap it again when you find the pop-up message.
  6. Sign in to your fitbit.com account.
  7. Personalize your Aria with a name and the initials you’d like the scale to display when it recognizes you.
  8. Remove a battery from your Aria scale and reinsert it after 10 seconds to put the scale into setup mode. Tap Continue when the scale’s display says “SETUP ACTIVE.”
  9. Switch your computer, phone, or tablet to the scale’s Wi-Fi network (this will appear as the word “Aria” followed by 6 characters).
  10. Return to your web browser and tap I’m Connected. You’ll find a list of available wireless networks.
  11. Tap the name of your home wireless network. If you can’t find your home wireless network, tap Refresh Networks to scan again. If you still can’t find your network, tap Join Other Network to enter your network name and password manually.
  12. Enter your network password. Remember that it’s case-sensitive.
  13. Tap Submit and then immediately check your scale’s screen as it attempts to connect to your network.
    • If you find a check mark or a smiley face, Aria is connected and you can stand on the scale to complete a weigh-in.
    • If you find an error message, go to How do I use my Fitbit scale?
Aria 2

To set up your Fitbit Aria 2, create an account. If you don’t have one, connect your scale through the Google Health app on your phone.

Router settings

Aria 2 connects to your wireless home network and works with any Wi-Fi router that uses these standards:

  • 802.11b/g/n frequency setting
  • WEP / WPA / WPA2 personal security
  • Automatic (DHCP) IP setup (static IP configurations aren’t supported)
  • Both the network name and password must be no more than 32 characters long

We don’t recommend a mobile Wi-Fi hotspot to set up Aria 2, as it may slow down the sync process and prevent an update. The use of a mobile Wi-Fi hotspot requires the device to remain persistently in this mode, which may drain the battery quickly and use excessive data.

  2. Download and install the Google Health app from the App Storeor Play Store.
  3. Open the Google app and tap Sign in with Google.
  4. Choose a Google Account. If you don’t have a Google Account, tap Sign in and then Create account.
  5. Follow the on-screen instructions to create a Google Health account and connect your scale to the internet. You must know your wireless network password and the scale must be within range of the network. If you find an error message, go to How do I use my Fitbit scale?

Note that the personal information you provide to set up your account is used to calculate your BMR. This helps determine your estimated calorie expenditure and your body mass index (BMI). For more information, go to How does my Fitbit device calculate my daily activity?

If you have trouble setting up Aria 2, briefly press the button in the battery compartment to restart your scale and begin the process again. If you still can’t set up your Aria 2 upon completion of the steps above, contact Customer Support.

If you have trouble setting up Aria 2, briefly press the button in the battery compartment to restart your scale and begin the setup process again.
